WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

YOUR ROLE

You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.

Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.

We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

  • Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier
  • Carrier conversion data running in production models
  • Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale
  • A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions
  • Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives
  • Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

  • 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact
  • Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.
  • You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included
  • You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift
  • You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view
  • Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

  • Real ad budget spent in live auctions
  • Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems
  • Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms
  • Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration
  • Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior
  • AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker
  • CI/CD deployment

jobs.description:
Application Deadline : 6 November - 17:00 CET

Contract Duration

One-year fixed term with possibility of extension or renewal

Language Proficiency

Fluency in spoken and written English. Working knowledge of French, Spanish or Portuguese would be an asset.

Location

Global, remote

Background

The Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) is an independent civil society organization headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, with a globally dispersed Secretariat working across 43 countries. Founded in 2013, GI-TOC brings together a global network of more than 810 independent experts and a team of over 150 staff dedicated to understanding and responding to organized crime. Through research, analysis, policy engagement and support to civil society actors, GI-TOC works to deepen understanding of organized crime and strengthen effective, rights-based responses.

The GI-TOC works to:

  • Identify, analyse and map criminal trends and patterns of regional instability, and their impact on illicit flows, governance, development, security, conflict and the rule of law.
  • Connect and support civil society actors working on organized crime and corruption, and on their links to instability and conflict.
  • Strengthen local monitoring and analysis of national, regional and international organized crime and insecurity trends.

Job Summary

GI-TOC is looking for an Monitoring Evaluation and Communications Officer to work across its two flagship environmental crime programmes. The role sits between programme administration and research, and needs both skill sets.

You will set up M&E systems across major projects in Latin America, Asia and Africa, working with environmental defenders, civil society organisations, law enforcement and the private sector. You will help build a body of practice on measuring the disruption of environmental crime networks and illicit economies, a field where good methods are still scarce. And you will make sure the impact of GI-TOC’s and its partners’ work reaches key audiences.

This is a growth role. Extensive M&E experience is not required, but you will be expected to upskill quickly and with dedication.

Main Responsibilities and Specific Tasks

  • Monitoring, evaluation and learning: set up M&E systems across projects; collect information to set and track baselines, targets and indicators across both programmes; review and evaluate narrative reports from partners, grantees and country teams; gather and write up stories of impact; and contribute to learning and impact reporting.
  • Measuring disruption: help build a body of practice on measuring the disruption of environmental crime networks and illicit economies.
  • Donor relations: support donor reporting and correspondence, and help keep commitments, deadlines and deliverables on track.
  • International coordination: support coordination across country teams, observatories and partners in Europe, Latin America, Africa and Asia.
  • Communications: make sure the impact of GI-TOC’s and partners’ work reaches key audiences, preparing summaries, impact stories, newsletters and briefing materials in liaison with GI-TOC’s communications team.
  • Bridging teams: act as a connector between programme, research, data and communications colleagues, and with close GI-TOC partners, so information flows and work is coherent across projects.

Required Skills and Experience

Essential

  • University degree in a relevant field.
  • Some professional experience in programme support, research, M&E or communications.
  • Familiarity with M&E concepts, practices and approaches, such as results frameworks, theories of change, indicators and outcome harvesting.
  • Excellent written English and the ability to turn complex information into clear material.
  • Highly organised, careful with detail, and able to manage several workstreams at once.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, and able to build relationships across teams and organisations

Desirable

  • Formal M&E training or experience on donor-funded programmes, especially EU or Norad.
  • Knowledge of environmental crime, organised crime or natural resource governance.
  • Experience producing communications content.
  • Working knowledge of French, Spanish or Portuguese.

Personal Attributes

We work best with people who take initiative, are creative but careful with detail, and have a strong drive to bring organisation and coherence to our projects and to pursue impact. You will need to be internally well networked, and comfortable working across teams, time zones and partners.

GI-TOC operates a flexible working environment and encourages staff to achieve a suitable work-life balance and supports professional development and learning.

Only short-listed candidates will be contacted.

About the Team

The IAM team is at the core of QuintoAndar's platform security. We build and maintain the systems that guarantee the right people and the right services have access to the right resources at the right time. We handle millions of authentication requests daily, and our services are the foundation of trust for the entire QuintoAndar ecosystem.


ResponsibilitiesThe Challenge At QuintoAndar, identity is our primary security perimeter. We are looking for a Sr. IAM Governance Analyst to evolve our access governance from a traditional, manual model to a "Continuous Compliance" ecosystem.

You won't be a traditional auditor focused merely on checking spreadsheet boxes. Your role will be strategic: designing access models (RBAC/ABAC), defining Segregation of Duties (SoD) matrices, and bridging the gap with our IAM Engineering team to transform security policies into automated controls (Paved Roads) using platforms like Okta.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Control & RBAC Design: Lead the modeling and standardization of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) profiles and Segregation of Duties (SoD) for critical systems and infrastructure.
  • Lifecycle Management (JML): Design the business rules for Joiner, Mover, and Leaver (JML) processes, ensuring the principle of least privilege without creating operational bottlenecks.
  • Compliance Automation (UAR): Orchestrate User Access Review (UAR) campaigns. Instead of manual processes, you will work closely with engineering to parameterize Okta and IAM Ecosystem, reducing friction and operational overhead for business managers.
  • Strategic Bridge: Act as the primary translator between Audit/GRC areas (SOX, LGPD, NIST) and technical Engineering squads (IAM/InfraSec), converting legal/regulatory requirements into actionable engineering user stories.
  • Continuous Auditing: Map residual risks in the identity ecosystem, develop actionable KPIs/KRIs, and proactively work with business units to mitigate orphaned accounts and over-provisioning.
  • Security Awareness & UX: Ensure IAM policies not only protect the company but also offer a seamless user experience for employees, adding friction only where strictly necessary.

What We Are Looking For (Requirements):

  • Solid, hands-on experience with IAM Governance principles: RBAC, ABAC, SoD, Least Privilege, and JML workflows.
  • Direct experience with the governance and parameterization of IGA and CIAM/Workforce platforms, such as SailPoint IdentityNow, Okta, CyberArk or others.
  • Engineering/Product mindset: The ability to look at manual governance processes and propose scalable, automated solutions.
  • Experience acting as the interface between business teams, external auditors, and software/security engineering teams.
  • Applied knowledge of security and compliance frameworks (NIST CSF, SOX, ISO 27001, LGPD/GDPR) specifically within the context of identity.
  • Strong analytical skills to cross-reference databases, identify access anomalies, and generate actionable metrics.
  • Exceptional and adaptable communication skills—you must be able to explain an SoD risk to an auditor and immediately pivot to discuss implementation feasibility with a developer.
  • Fluency in Portuguese and advanced knowledge of English.

We will like you even more if you have:

JOIN THE COME AND SEE TEAM

Controller

Colorado Springs, CO or Remote (U.S.) • Full-time • Finance

The greatest story ever told deserves financial stewardship worthy of it, and the people who steward it well deserve to be trusted with real ownership. If you find genuine satisfaction in a clean close, airtight controls, and numbers that tell the truth — we would love to meet you.

ABOUT US

Come and See is the faith-based nonprofit media ministry behind The Chosen. Our mission is inviting everyone to encounter Jesus through exceptional storytelling that brings the Bible to life. From funding production of the series to translating every season into 600 languages and making it freely available around the world, our Team Members work together as collaborators in the greatest mission on earth. And we are just getting started!

ABOUT THE ROLE

As our Controller, you will own the accounting operation behind our mission — the close, the controls, the audit, and the financial reporting our Board, auditors, and donors rely on. You will bring the technical judgment that stands behind our financial statements, turning the generosity entrusted to us into reporting that is accurate, timely, and built to last.

As Come and See has grown, so has the complexity of how we account for it — donor-restricted giving across four Pillars, production funding, translation and localization work across many languages and currencies, and a growing, distributed team. You will bring order and rigor to that complexity, freeing our CFO to focus on strategy and Board-level leadership.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will be close enough to the ledger to know when something is off, and senior enough to fix the process that caused it. When our CFO is away, you will hold the finance function.

We are also looking for someone as comfortable leveraging AI-powered tools to streamline financial operations as they are with traditional close processes and GAAP compliance — using AI copilots for reconciliations, variance analysis, and reporting, while maintaining the rigor and judgment only an experienced finance leader brings.

You will report to the Chief Financial Officer.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the close. Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual close, delivering reviewed financial statements under U.S. GAAP for not-for-profits (ASC 958) on an agreed timeline, with variance explanations.
  • Steward the ledger. Own the general ledger, chart of accounts, net asset classification, and functional expense allocation methodology.
  • Lead reporting and budgeting. Produce reporting packages for the CFO, executive team, and Board Finance/Audit Committee; lead the annual budget process and budget-to-actual reporting.
  • Own technical accounting. Handle contributions, grants, royalties, and rebates, including conditional vs. unconditional determinations; research complex or novel transactions and bring well-supported recommendations.
  • Keep donor and financial data in sync. Maintain the reconciliation between our donor CRM and the general ledger, and maintain project-level accounting so spend can be reported against the Pillar it serves.
  • Lead the audit. Serve as primary auditor contact for our annual external audit; evaluate and respond to proposed adjustments.
  • Design our controls. Build and enforce internal controls over financial reporting, including segregation of duties, banking access, payment approvals, and fraud prevention.
  • Own compliance. Maintain charitable solicitation, state tax, and multi-state registrations; monitor unrelated business income.
  • Authorize payroll. Serve as the final authorization point for each payroll cycle — reviewing the register prepared by People & Culture, resolving exceptions, and releasing payroll. You will authorize, not prepare.
  • Oversee AP and contractors. Own accounts payable, expense reimbursement, corporate cards, the vendor master file, and contractor payments, including 1099 reporting.
  • Lead and develop the team. Coach the accounting team, build cross-training, and serve as the CFO's primary back-up during absences.
  • Modernize how we work. Own our financial systems environment and lead automation — including AI-enabled tools — that reduces manual reconciliation and control risk.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting and an active CPA license.
  • Minimum 7 years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 5 years in a not-for-profit organization.
  • Experience leading and developing accounting staff.
  • Working depth in not-for-profit GAAP (ASC 958): net assets, functional expense allocation, and contribution revenue.
  • Demonstrated ownership of a full-cycle monthly close and an annual external audit.
  • Experience designing internal controls in a lean organization, where segregation of duties must be engineered thoughtfully.
  • Multi-state payroll tax and contractor/1099 knowledge; fluency in a mid-market ERP and advanced Excel.
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar) to accelerate financial analysis, draft reports, or automate repetitive accounting tasks, with sound judgment about where human review and controls remain essential.
  • A clear communicator with non-financial leaders, comfortable working in a remote, distributed team.
  • A personal faith in Jesus and alignment with our mission, values, and Statement of Faith.

BONUS POINTS

  • Experience in media, entertainment, or content production/distribution.
  • Prior Controller or Assistant Controller experience in a donor-funded organization.
  • Multi-currency and international payments experience.
  • Experience evaluating or implementing AI-enabled finance tools (automated reconciliation, AI-assisted forecasting, intelligent document processing).

WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING HERE

  • Meaningful work. Your work directly protects and strengthens the financial foundation behind The Chosen's reach around the world.
  • Real trust. You won't just maintain the books — you'll shape the controls, systems, and processes that carry this mission forward.
  • Room to grow. Come and See is growing, and the complexity and scope of this role will grow with it.
  • Remote flexibility. Work from Colorado Springs or remotely from anywhere in the U.S., with occasional in-person gatherings.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Salary Range , $128,000 to $168,000 per year, based on experience and qualifications

FLSA Classification , Exempt

Benefits , Medical, dental, vision, retirement plan and match, HRA, Short and Long-term Disability, Group Life and Voluntary Life Insurance, generous and flexible holidays, and more.

OUR BELIEFS, CULTURE, AND COMMITMENT

At Come and See, every team member plays a vital role in a mission bigger than any one of us. We look for passion for the mission and a genuine capacity to represent our culture and Christian beliefs throughout the selection process for every role. Wherever we serve, we aim to uphold and reflect Jesus in how we live and work together.

While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn't mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team with people from all backgrounds. We believe that varied perspectives — across race, ethnicity, life experience, age, and gender — enrich our ability to share the story of Jesus with the world and help everyone, everywhere, experience the authentic Jesus.

HOW TO APPLY

Submit your resume and a cover letter telling us why this role and our mission resonate with you. Application deadline: October 31, 2026.

OUR COMMITTMENT

Come and See is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. As a religious organization, Come and See lawfully exercises its right under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and applicable state law to employ individuals who share its religious beliefs.

Come and See is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified applicants. If you need an accommodation during the application process, please contact

jobs.excerpt: ✨ About the CompanyMakeship empowers influencers, creators, and brands of all sizes to develop and launch limited-edition products that matter to their fans.
jobs.description:
✨ About the Company

Makeship empowers influencers, creators, and brands of all sizes to develop and launch limited-edition products that matter to their fans. Leveraging our design, manufacturing, and marketing expertise, we work with our partners to bring their products to life through our community-powered crowdfunding platform. Each product is given a window of 21 days to be funded by the community before we produce and ship to fans worldwide. We put our brand behind every product and guarantee quality and ethical sourcing.

We're profitable; we have a three-year revenue growth of over 200%, ranking us 97th in 2024 and 86th on The Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies of 2025 list. In 2025 alone, our sales exceeded $65M CAD. We are proud to be Great Place to Work-Certified™ for 3 years in a row! Learn more about us at Makeship.com.

🧑‍💻 About the Role

We are looking for a Sales Strategy & Enablement Lead who can take what great selling looks like here, sharpen it, scale it, and keep evolving it as we grow. This is a role for someone who understands people deeply. You know how to build trust fast, uncover what actually matters, make a value proposition click, handle objections before they become roadblocks, and tell a story that people remember.

But you’re not just a great seller.

You know how to turn instinct into something teachable.

You can listen to a call and immediately hear what landed, what didn’t, and what should change. You can rewrite the deck, sharpen the talk track, rethink the follow-up, coach the AE, and then look at the data to see whether it worked.
You won’t carry an individual quota. Your impact will show up in the performance of the entire Partnerships team.

Reporting to the VP, Revenue, you’ll own how we approach, pitch, nurture, win, grow, and win back Creator relationships. Your closest business partner will be our Sales Manager, who owns day-to-day team leadership and performance. You’ll also work closely with RevOps, Marketing, Data, and teams across Makeship.

This is not a role where you sit on the sidelines and hand people frameworks.

You’ll be in sales calls. You’ll talk to Creators. You’ll coach AEs. You’ll challenge assumptions. You’ll test ideas. You’ll throw out what isn’t working. And when something starts working really well, you’ll figure out how to make the whole team better at it.

Makeship already has six years of learning, strong growth, and a lot that works. Your job is to understand why it works, make it better, and evolve it as we launch new products, enter new Creator verticals, and keep raising the bar.

🌟 What We Are Looking For

We’re looking for a salesperson first.

Someone with exceptional EQ, strong instincts, competitive energy, and a genuine understanding of how language, trust, relationships, and timing influence a sale.

You may be a top-performing AE, a sales strategy or enablement lead, or the person other sellers naturally come to when they need help closing something difficult. You may have built playbooks, mentored teammates, or moved into sales leadership.

Your title matters less to us than the pattern.

You’ve sold. You’ve learned what works. You’ve developed your own judgment. And at some point, you realized you were just as excited about making the team better as you were about winning the deal yourself.

Creator economy experience is a major advantage. Selling to Creators is not traditional B2B sales. Relationships are built through Instagram, Discord, YouTube, calls, DMs, and communities as often as they are through formal meetings.
You need to be comfortable in that world; or, come from another fast-moving, relationship-led environment where you’ve learned how to sell without hiding behind a rigid corporate playbook.

We move quickly. We’re competitive. We’re curious. We challenge each other, laugh a lot, and care deeply about doing great work. You should be confident enough to work independently, humble enough to change your mind, and comfortable jumping from a strategic conversation straight into the weeds.

🚀 Your Key Responsibilities

Sales Storytelling & Methodology:

Own and continuously evolve how Makeship sells.

  • Turn Makeship’s value proposition, results, capabilities, and differentiators into a clear, memorable sales story.
  • Personally develop and improve sales decks, talk tracks, discovery frameworks, pitch approaches, objection handling, nurture messaging, follow-up strategies, and playbooks.
  • Help AEs and AMs understand not just what to say, but why it works and how to adapt the story to the Creator in front of them.
  • Build a methodology flexible enough for emerging Creators, established Creators, and different Creator verticals.
  • Adapt our approach as Makeship launches new products, enters new Creator verticals, or tests new ways of working with Creators.

Coaching & Enablement:

Make the team better at selling.

  • Work directly with AEs through live coaching, call reviews, workshops, pitch development, and ongoing feedback.
  • Own our sales enablement program, including onboarding, recurring training, playbooks, workshops, and certification.
  • Partner closely with the Sales Manager so the methodology becomes part of ongoing team coaching.
    Identify what our strongest sellers are doing differently and make those behaviours repeatable across the team.

Creator Growth & Relationship Strategy:

Help us sell beyond the first drop in the Creator's best interest.

  • Build frameworks that help AMs move from “we need another launch” to thoughtful Creator growth planning.
  • Help define how teams should think about timing, product progression, Creator milestones, fan moments, tentpoles, and larger programs.
  • Develop the questions, planning tools, and storytelling that help AMs build strategic roadmaps with Creators.
  • Create win-back approaches for Creators whose relationship with Makeship has lapsed.
    Help the team understand how a great fan experience should influence what we recommend to Creators.

Competitive Strategy:

Make sure our team knows why Makeship wins.

  • Stay close to competitors, their positioning, their offers, and changes in the Creator merchandise space.
  • Turn competitive insight into better discovery, positioning, talk tracks, objection handling, and sales plays.
  • Teach AEs and AMs how to recognize competitive threats, uncover weaknesses, and position Makeship naturally and confidently.
  • Help build a team that knows how to assess the landscape in real time rather than relying on a static battlecard.

Testing, Data & Continuous Improvement:

Keep learning what works.

  • Stay close to frontline conversations and use them to form hypotheses about what could make us better.
  • Use funnel and performance data to understand what’s improving, where momentum is breaking down, and what to test next.
  • Track signals including win rate, conversion, sales-cycle length, speed to first launch, repeat launches, expansion, and other measures of sales effectiveness.
  • Work with RevOps and Data to define the reporting and insights you need.
  • Test changes in messaging, follow-up, sequencing, pitch structure, and methodology, then keep what works and change what doesn’t.

Revenue Operations & Marketing Partnership:

Know what great selling needs, then help the right teams build it.

  • Partner with RevOps on the sequences, workflows, CRM support, alerts, and tools that reinforce the sales methodology.
  • Be comfortable working in HubSpot and hands-on enough to build or test simpler solutions yourself when it makes sense.
  • Bring forward new sales technology when you believe it can make the team more effective.
  • Partner with Marketing so Creator-facing content reinforces the same story our team is telling in the field.
  • Identify the content and assets the sales team needs — from proof points and case studies to videos and Creator education — and work with Marketing to bring them to life.
  • Bring frontline Creator insights back into the business so our broader messaging keeps getting stronger.

🧠 What You Bring

  • 7+ years of sales experience, including significant time in a quota-carrying role, with strong live selling instincts and a track record of building trust fast, uncovering motivation, and adapting quickly.
  • Evidence that you've made other sellers better through mentoring, coaching, sales leadership, or enablement.
  • The ability to turn a complex value proposition into a simple, memorable story, and to build the practical tools that help others tell it, such as talk tracks, pitch decks, discovery frameworks, objection handling, and follow-up strategies.
  • Experience in a startup, scale-up, or emerging category where the playbook was still being written, and a natural instinct to turn ambiguity into something clearer and more useful.
  • Strong competitive instincts and curiosity about why buyers choose one option over another.
  • Comfort interpreting sales funnel data and working in CRM and sales technology (ideally HubSpot) to improve performance.
  • A collaborative, low-ego approach and the confidence to challenge an idea when you see a better one.

👀 Bonus

  • Experience selling to Creators, influencers, talent, communities, or other non-traditional business owners.
  • Experience in the Creator economy, gaming, merchandise, crowdfunding, fandom-led commerce, or another community-driven industry.
  • Experience adapting your sales approach across audience segments and verticals, from informal, relationship-led conversations to larger strategic accounts.
  • Previous experience as a sales leader, or building and evolving a sales enablement program in a high-growth startup.
  • Confidence speaking to groups, facilitating workshops, or representing a company externally.

🎁 Benefits & Perks

  • Work remotely anywhere in Canada and/or access any of our hubs
  • Health and dental benefits from day 1
  • 4 weeks of paid vacation (including paid time off on your birthday)
  • An additional 1 week of paid time off during the winter holidays
  • Virtual & In-Person Social Events
  • Annual Paid Volunteer Day Off
  • 1:1 RRSP Matching Program Up to 3%
  • $500 Pre-Tax Annual Health & Wellness Allowance
  • $400 Pre-Tax Home Office Setup Allowance
  • $65 Pre-Tax Monthly Phone Allowance
  • Maternity and Parental Leave Top-Up Program
  • Education Assistance Program
  • Employee Referral Program
  • Tenured Rewards Program

Salary Band: $90-100K CAD base salary per annum, plus a variable of $30-40K CAD, for an OTE of $120-140K CAD. Individual compensation will depend on unique skills, experience, and qualifications.

Vacancy Status: Existing vacancy

AI Use Disclosure:
As part of our hiring process, we may use AI-powered tools to support tasks such as application screening and note-taking. These tools are used to assist our team, andall hiring decisions are made by humans.

We are committed to fair and unbiased hiring practices. If you require accommodations or have questions about how your application is assessed, please let us know.

At Makeship we are committed to fostering an environment that welcomes people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities. We are passionate about building an equitable and inclusive culture for our unique and diverse team of employees which makes us Makeship. As an equal-opportunity employer, we value and embrace everyone's opinions and differences, and actively seek new Makeshippers who will work respectfully with our team, propelling our company and the community forward. If there are any accommodations we can provide to make your interview experience more accessible and inclusive, please let us know in your application.

About Us

Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 80 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.

Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.
Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.

About the Role

Bybit EU is looking for the Head for Commercial / Business Developmentto lead our European commercial strategy, market expansion and revenue growth across regulated digital asset and financial services.
Reporting directly to the EU Group CEO, you will lead the European commercial organisation, including Country Managers and their respective in-country Business Development, KOL, VIP Relationship Management and Community teams. You will work closely with Marketing, Product, Operations, Compliance and global Commercial teams to drive growth across European markets.

Key Responsibilities

Commercial Strategy & Growth

  • Define and execute the European commercial strategy aligned with business objectives, market opportunities and regulatory requirements.
  • Own commercial targets, revenue growth, trading volumes, customer acquisition and market expansion.
  • Identify strategic growth opportunities across retail, active trader, VIP and institutional customer segments.

Country Management & Market Expansion

  • Define country-specific business plans, growth targets and market development priorities.
  • Oversee in-country commercial activities, including business development, partnerships, KOL engagement, VIP relationships and community management.
  • Monitor country performance, competitive positioning and market opportunities to optimise commercial results.

Business Development & Partnerships

  • Drive business development initiatives to expand Bybit EU's customer base, trading activity and market presence.
  • Develop strategic commercial partnerships with relevant fintech, crypto, trading and financial services ecosystems.

KOL, Affiliate & Community Development

VIP & Key Account Management

  • Drive trading activity, customer loyalty and revenue growth through personalised relationship management.

Commercial Performance & Governance

  • Own commercial budgets, sales forecasts, revenue reporting and performance management across European markets.

  • Ensure commercial activities, partnerships and customer engagement comply with applicable European regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Compliance, Risk and Legal to maintain appropriate governance over commercial activities and customer relationships.

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Build and lead a high-performing European commercial organisation, including Country Managers, Business Development, KOL, VIP Relationship Management and Community teams.
  • Set clear objectives, performance targets and accountability across country and commercial functions.
  • Act as a key member of the European executive leadership team, contributing to business strategy and sustainable growth.
  • Collaborate with global and local stakeholders to align commercial initiatives with European market needs and regulatory requirements.

What We're Looking For

  • 15+ years of relevant experience in commercial leadership, business development, sales or market expansion, including significant executive experience in crypto, fintech, trading, brokerage or financial services.
  • Proven experience leading multi-country commercial organisations and delivering sustainable revenue growth across European markets.
  • Strong understanding of crypto trading, digital assets, derivatives and financial services customer segments.
  • Demonstrated experience managing Country Managers, business development teams and international commercial operations.
  • Strong experience developing KOL, affiliate, community and strategic partnership networks within the crypto or trading ecosystem.

  • Strong commercial and analytical mindset with experience managing revenue, trading volumes, customer acquisition, retention and profitability metrics.
  • Experience developing market entry strategies, commercial partnerships and country-specific growth plans.
  • Strong understanding of European markets, regulatory requirements and customer engagement within regulated financial services environments.
  • Proven ability to build high-performing international teams and manage complex stakeholder relationships.

  • Fluent English; additional European languages are an advantage
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Marketing, Management or a related field; equivalent relevant professional experience will also be considered.

Why Join Us
At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment.

Our benefits include:

jobs.description:
Game Engineer (remote, contract-to-hire, Latin America)

Location: Latin America preferred (remote)

Reports to: Director of Technical Production

Engagement type: Full-time contract (40 hours/week), 5–6 months, with the intent to convert to a long-term role

Language requirement: Professional or fluent in English; Spanish preferred

About Endless Access

Our vision is simple: the whole world, empowered.

Endless Access works to close the global digital divide by helping young people in underserved communities become creators of technology, not only consumers of it. Our learning programs teach a new generation to design and build their own games and digital projects using free, open-source tools, delivered through mentors, instructors, and partners around the world.

These learning programs center around our flagship game, Threadbare. Students develop their skills and ambitions as they transition from playing the game to helping build it. Threadbare is developed in the open, by our Games team and a growing community of contributors. As our programs reach more learners in more regions, we are growing the team that keeps the game stable, fun, and welcoming to the people learning to build it.

About the Role

Endless Access is seeking a mid-level Game Engineer, based in Latin America, to join our Games team and help build Threadbare, an open-source, community-built narrative adventure game made with the Godot engine. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will ship features, fix issues, and help keep the game stable, performant, and fun to play.

You will work closely with our senior game engineer as well as our creative director, producer, and contributor community. Most of your time will go to game development on the Threadbare roadmap. A smaller part of the role connects you with our learning programs, where you will guide learners who are building the game alongside us.

This is a 5–6 month contract, and we are hiring with the clear intent of finding someone we would want on the team long term.

If you enjoy working in an existing codebase, care about how changes feel to players, and like helping newer developers grow, this role is for you.

Key Responsibilities

Game Development (60%)

  • Build and ship gameplay features, UI, and systems, from design spec to release.
  • Fix bugs and improve performance, stability, and load times.
  • Work with design and art to turn ideas into playable builds, and give feedback on feasibility and scope.
  • Write clean, tested, maintainable code, and take part in code reviews with the team.
  • Estimate your work, flag risks early, and keep the team informed through planning and regular updates.
  • Contribute to the tools, pipelines, and documentation that make the team faster.

Learning and Community (40%)

  • Review code from learners in our game development programs and give clear, encouraging written feedback.
  • Collaborate with our Learning Experience team on tooling that supports our game development curriculum, as the roadmap allows.
  • Join occasional community events, such as game jams and livestreams.

Skills and Experience

Essential

  • 4+ years of professional software engineering, including hands-on work on shipped or live games.
  • Experience shipping or maintaining a released game or live product as part of a team, working alongside other engineers, designers, and artists.
  • Comfortable with Git-based workflows, code review, and working in an existing codebase.
  • Willingness to mentor early-career game developers by reviewing their code and giving written feedback.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, especially in a remote, asynchronous team.
  • Familiarity with open-source communities and contribution practices.
  • Able to work independently and to ask for help at the right time.
  • Professional or fluent English.

Desirable

  • Experience with the Godot engine (GDScript)
  • Accessibility or inclusive design experience in games.
  • Experience with learning or educational games.
  • Familiarity with analytics, live ops, or build and CI pipelines.
  • Spanish ability.
  • An interest in our mission to expand access to technology.

How We Work

Endless Access is a fully distributed, global nonprofit. Most of the team works remotely and asynchronously across many countries, and this role is no exception: it is fully remote and based in Latin America, collaborating daily with teammates and contributors across multiple time zones, much of it in writing, in code review, and over video. We are looking for someone who thrives in a self-directed, cross-cultural environment, and who communicates clearly and openly in writing.

Not Sure You Meet 100% of the Requirements?

Studies show that women and people from underrepresented backgrounds often hesitate to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. Building a truly inclusive digital future means bringing together diverse perspectives and experiences; if you are excited about this role and our mission to expand access to technology, we strongly encourage you to apply even if you do not check every box. jobs.excerpt: Applications for this position will be accepted through 11/15/26 Koniag IT Systems, LLC a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking a CDO-L Study Lead Engineer with a Secret security clearance to support KITS and our government customer.
jobs.description:
Applications for this position will be accepted through 11/15/26 Koniag IT Systems, LLC a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking a CDO-L Study Lead Engineer with a Secret security clearance to support KITS and our government customer. The position is remote.

Koniag IT Systems, LLC a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking an experienced CDO-L Study Lead Engineer to support the Department of the Air Force (DAF) in advancing its enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) capabilities. This position will lead a focused, technically grounded study effort under Task Order 0003, System Enhancement Studies, with a primary focus on extending secure ICAM capabilities into Contested, Degraded, and Operationally Limited (CDO-L) environments. The ideal candidate is a technically seasoned engineer and collaborative leader with deep experience in Defense ICAM architectures, Zero Trust frameworks, and disconnected/edge identity solutions who can translate complex operational requirements into actionable architectures and implementation roadmaps.

  • This study will run 120 days. All personnel assigned to CDO-L study activities must hold a final Secret security clearance.

The CDO-L Study Lead Engineer will serve as the primary technical authority for Study 1 of the DAF ICAM System Enhancement Studies effort, leading the analysis, architecture development, and documentation required to produce a decision-ready Technical Study Report within 45 calendar days of Task Order award. The Lead Engineer will coordinate closely with the Program Manager, Systems Architecture Team, Licensing/Cost Analyst, and Government stakeholders to ensure all study outputs are technically sound, operationally grounded, and fully traceable to Performance Work Statement (PWS) Section 4.1 requirements.

Principal responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

  • Lead the structured review of Government-provided CDO-L requirements published at the DoD Enterprise ICAM IL5 and IL6 DDIL reference site, cataloging each requirement by operational condition (denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited bandwidth) and mapping them against existing DAF ICAM solution components including Okta Universal Directory (UD), Okta Identity Provider (IdP), and SailPoint IdentityIQ (IIQ).
  • Conduct a gap analysis between current DAF ICAM capabilities and CDO-L operational demands to serve as the foundation for all architectural recommendations.
  • Evaluate existing approved ICAM solutions across comparable Federal Defense programs and assess their applicability to DAF CDO-L requirements, prioritizing solutions that extend existing approved capabilities rather than introducing net-new vendor stacks.
  • Lead the architectural analysis of options for on-premises replication or caching of identity and access data at disconnected nodes, evaluating a tiered edge identity broker model across three operational states: Connected, Degraded/Limited Bandwidth, and Denied.
  • Assess and document synchronization schedules, minimum connectivity requirements, degraded-mode operating parameters, and cache staleness thresholds for each operational state.
  • Evaluate specific DAF ICAM-aligned edge components including Okta Access Gateway (OAG) and Tactical Identity Bridge Appliance (TIBA) for their suitability in extending ICAM operations to the tactical edge.
  • Assess how existing SailPoint IIQ governance workflows can be mirrored at the edge to maintain entitlement integrity during disconnected operations.
  • Document tradeoffs between full replication, selective caching, and read-only policy mirroring, and provide a recommended approach with clear technical rationale grounded in DAF operational requirements.
  • Develop recommendations for emergency "break-glass" access provisioning in fully offline or denied-state conditions, including governance controls, immutable local audit logging, and automated revocation and re-synchronization workflows.
  • Evaluate approaches for PKI certificate validation in CDO-L conditions, including Certificate Revocation List (CRL) caching and local Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) stapling at edge nodes to sustain Common Access Card (CAC)-based authentication.
  • Analyze how endpoint security telemetry collected locally during a disconnected period integrates with the identity layer and how the edge identity broker can autonomously enforce access revocation when device security posture degrades.
  • Develop a formal methodology for attribute transfer and synchronization between enterprise NIPRNet and SIPRNet environments and disconnected nodes upon reconnection, addressing conflict resolution, synchronization priorities, audit log consolidation, reconciliation validation, and failure/fallback procedures.
  • Coordinate with the Licensing/Cost Analyst to produce a structured identification of all software components required for the recommended CDO-L architecture, including licensing structure, edge deployment constraints, classified-network restrictions, and interoperability considerations.
  • Coordinate with the Program Manager and Licensing/Cost Analyst to develop a detailed, phased implementation roadmap and ROM cost estimate covering development, licensing, hardware, integration, testing, and deployment.
  • Consolidate all study outputs into the CDO-L Technical Study Report (CDRL B010), ensuring each section maps directly to a PWS Section 4.1 requirement and includes a draft Performance Work Statement suitable for a subsequent implementation Task Order.
  • Verify that all assigned personnel hold the required security clearances prior to engagement and notify the Government immediately of any clearance status changes.
  • Present study findings to Government Program Manager and Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) as required throughout the study period.

Education and Experience:

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field from an accredited college or university.
  • 7+ years of experience in systems engineering, enterprise architecture, or identity and access management within Defense or Federal government IT environments.
  • Demonstrated experience designing or analyzing identity and access management architectures in disconnected, air-gapped, or operationally constrained network environments.
  • Experience with the DoD Authority to Operate (ATO) process and security accreditation requirements for Defense information systems.
  • Active Secret security clearance (final adjudication required prior to assignment).

Preferred:

  • Master's degree in a related technical field.
  • 10+ years of experience in Defense ICAM, enterprise identity architecture, or related cybersecurity engineering disciplines.
  • Experience supporting DISA-aligned programs or DAF/Air Force ICAM initiatives.

Required Skills and Competencies:

  • Deep technical knowledge of enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) platforms, with specific expertise in Okta (Universal Directory, Identity Provider, Access Gateway, Workflows) and SailPoint IdentityIQ (IIQ).
  • Strong understanding of Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles and their application to tactical edge and disconnected identity environments.
  • Experience designing identity federation, replication, and caching architectures for disconnected or intermittently connected operational environments.
  • Proficiency in PKI-based authentication concepts, including Certificate Revocation Lists (CRL), Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP), and Common Access Card (CAC) authentication.
  • Knowledge of Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) policy frameworks and their implementation within Okta and SailPoint platforms.
  • Familiarity with NIPRNet and SIPRNet network architecture, classification requirements, and cross-domain constraints.
  • Ability to perform and document structured gap analyses, architectural tradeoff assessments, and comparative technology evaluations.
  • Experience developing phased implementation roadmaps with clearly defined entry/exit criteria, dependencies, and realistic Government review and accreditation timelines.
  • Strong technical writing skills with the ability to produce formal study reports, architectural documentation, and draft Performance Work Statements suitable for Government use.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across cross-functional technical teams including architects, engineers, cost analysts, and program managers.
  • Exceptional communication skills in English—both written and oral—with the ability to present complex technical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical Government stakeholders.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance.

Desired Skills and Competencies:

  • Experience with Okta Access Gateway (OAG) and/or Tactical Identity Bridge Appliance (TIBA) in edge deployment contexts.
  • Familiarity with DoD Enterprise ICAM IL5/IL6 DDIL requirements and related DoD ICAM policy frameworks.
  • Knowledge of emergency "break-glass" access provisioning governance and associated audit/logging requirements in classified environments.
  • Experience integrating endpoint security telemetry with identity and access management platforms for continuous posture-based access enforcement.
  • Familiarity with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems and audit log consolidation in Defense environments.
  • Knowledge of Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and their application to identity platform components.
  • Experience developing Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimates for complex, multi-phase Defense IT implementation programs.
  • Okta Certified Professional, Okta Certified Administrator, SailPoint Certified IdentityIQ Engineer, or equivalent identity platform certification.
  • CISSP, CISM, or equivalent cybersecurity certification.
  • Experience supporting DAF, Air Force, or Space Force IT modernization programs.
  • Familiarity with Agile development methodologies and their application within hybrid Agile/Waterfall Government program environments.

Frontier is a subsidiary of Fresh Prints. Fresh Prints is a New York-based, fast-growing, fully remote, 150-person company with most of our team based in India and the Philippines. A few years ago, Fresh Prints began helping other fast-growing companies build their teams. We got so good at it that we spun out a new company to focus exclusively on that — and called it Frontier.

We help companies grow cross-functional teams abroad. We hire the smartest people and place them into great companies. If you're interested in a Frontier role and you apply and are accepted, we'll screen you through assessments and interviews and aim to connect you with the right opportunity.

About the client

Balto’s mission is to power a new era of knowledge work in the contact center, and we're creating awesome technology to do just that. If you're excited by the opportunity to join a dynamic team initiating a technological revolution in Real-Time Guidance, Balto is for you.

More than just a company, Balto is a community. A community committed to empowering each of our members. This mission is at the heart of our organization. As a member of our Technical Success team, you’ll act as the voice of the user, drive efficient implementation & product engagement from onboarding to continued adoption, and investigate solutions for complex technical issues.

We are looking a Technical Success Specialist to join Balto's Support team. In this role, you will serve as the primary internal escalation point for Support's most complex, multi-part customer issues, owning them from investigation through resolution, and acting as the buffer between Support and Engineering so that only genuinely engineering-level problems consume engineering time.

Responsibilities

  • Investigate and resolve customer inquiries regarding Balto products and services
  • Interact with customers through email and video conferencing
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Customer Success Managers, Implementation Managers, and the Sales Team to handle a variety of post-sales service functions
  • Investigate reported technical issues to discover root causes and find solutions
  • Provide ongoing support to customers for technical issues, including talking customers through a series of actions to resolve a problem, and then following up to ensure the problem is resolved
  • Log all calls and support requests
  • Technical documentation development for both internal and external audiences
  • Help make our integrations successful:
  • Troubleshoot complex integration issues
  • Conduct post-live integration checks during low implementation manager bandwidth periods

Job specific requirements

  • Strong troubleshooting and deductive reasoning
  • Highly organized and methodical
  • Comfortable in a customer-facing role
  • Knowledgeable in networking, firewall, and VPN
  • Clear and concise verbal and written communications
  • Great rapport-building skills
  • Ability to contribute and adapt to evolving support procedures
  • Very comfortable in Windows (10+) and MacOS environments
  • Knowledge or experience related to CCaaS or VoIP softphone applications highly desired, but not required
  • Experience writing, reading, or editing common coding languages a plus (Python, JSON, etc.)
  • Experience writing, reading, or editing code in a web environment a plus (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, etc.)
  • Experience with DataDog highly desired, but not required

Compensation & Benefits

  • $650- $800
  • A robust vacation and PTO schedule
  • You will be working in the US shift timings

Principal Java Developer – Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Principal Java Developer
Location: 100% Remote (United States)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $120,000–$170,000 Annually
Experience: 12+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are seeking an accomplished Java Full Stack Developer to architect, design, develop, and maintain enterprise-grade web applications and distributed systems that operate at significant scale and across multiple business domains. In this role you will be responsible for the end-to-end engineering lifecycle, from translating business requirements into robust technical designs, to writing production-quality code, to deploying cloud-native services and supporting them through their full operational lifespan. The successful candidate will bring deep backend expertise in Java and the Spring ecosystem, combined with strong hands-on experience building responsive, component-driven front-end applications using modern JavaScript frameworks. You will work closely with product managers, architects, DevOps engineers, and fellow developers in an Agile environment to deliver high-quality, secure, and performant applications that directly support strategic business outcomes.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
  • 12 or more years of professional software development experience building production-grade enterprise applications.
  • Strong, demonstrable understanding of data structures, algorithms, computational complexity, and end-to-end system design principles.
  • Advanced working knowledge of Java (versions 11 and 17), the Spring Boot framework, and the design of clean, idiomatic RESTful APIs.
  • Hands-on, production-level experience designing and operating microservices architectures, including service decomposition, inter-service communication, and observability patterns.
  • Proven experience developing front-end applications using React, with working familiarity in Angular or Vue considered a strong plus.
  • Strong SQL skills and meaningful experience working with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, or SQL Server, including query tuning and schema design.
  • Solid experience with CI/CD tooling and Git-based version control workflows, including branching strategies, code review practices, and release management.
  • Hands-on experience deploying applications to at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including familiarity with managed services, networking, and identity primitives.
  • Strong debugging, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis skills, with the discipline to investigate problems methodically and document findings clearly.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience designing and operating event-driven architectures using Kafka, RabbitMQ, or equivalent streaming platforms.
  • Familiarity with containerization and orchestration using Docker and Kubernetes in production environments.
  • Exposure to distributed system design principles such as eventual consistency, CAP trade-offs, idempotency, and saga patterns.
  • Experience writing automation tests using modern frameworks and contributing to test-driven and behavior-driven development practices.
How to Apply
Would you like to know more about this opportunity? For immediate consideration, please send your resume to  or contact us at (908) 505-3899. Learn more about Bright Vision Technologies at www.bvteck.com.

jobs.description:
ITHAKA’s mission is to expand access to knowledge and education around the world. Our services — JSTOR, Portico, and Ithaka S+R — enable people everywhere to learn, to grow, and to overcome barriers to education. In carrying out our mission, as employees we feel a deep responsibility to members of our community and to each other, and we are committed to building and sustaining a culture where everyone can thrive.

The Role

ITHAKA is seeking a Lead Software Engineer, Platform Engineering (Full-Stack) to advance how software is built, delivered, and experienced across the product engineering organization. This role sits on the Technology Enabling Services team and combines full-stack product engineering with DevOps and platform enablement, with a strong emphasis on developer experience, usability, and operational excellence.

You will design, build, and operate internal platforms, tools, and services that empower engineering teams to deliver high-quality software faster and more safely. This includes hands-on development of backend services, CI/CD and automation capabilities, and intuitive user-facing interfaces and internal web applications. Your work will directly influence how developers interact with our platforms and how effectively teams ship and maintain software. This is a highly collaborative role for a senior engineer who enjoys building production systems, mentoring others, shaping engineering practices, and acting as a force multiplier across teams.

Responsibilities

  • Architect, develop, and maintain internal platforms, services, and tooling that support CI/CD, automation, and software delivery.
  • Drive the product life cycle of the development platform including CI/CD pipelines, deployment strategies, platform automation, and productivity tooling.
  • Understand developer needs, and apply DevOps and enablement methodologies to improve development velocity, reliability, quality, and operational efficiency through paved paths.
  • Partner closely with product, platform, and application engineering teams to improve developer workflows and platform usability.
  • Champion developer experience by ensuring enablement tools are intuitive, accessible, well-documented, and aligned with user needs.
  • Mentor and coach engineers across teams on architecture, coding standards, DevOps practices, and UI/UX considerations.
  • Facilitate technical deep dives, design reviews, and training sessions to promote shared learning and best practices.
  • Practice strong portfolio management, including assessing, prototyping, trialing, implementing, and sunsetting technologies as fit for purpose.
  • Collaborate to develop internal platform roadmaps and help translate organizational goals into actionable technical initiatives.
  • Operate with a “You Build It, You Own It” mindset, taking shared responsibility for the reliability, maintainability, security, and evolution of the code you help put into production.
  • Participate in incident response, production support, troubleshooting, and follow-up remediation.
  • Improve practices for availability, alerting, performance, capacity, cost, recovery, and technical debt.
  • Turn operational learning into improvements to the platform and the way it is used.

Experience and Skills

We do not expect any single candidate to have deep expertise across all of these areas. We are looking for engineers who value continuous improvement and who focus on building clear, reliable, and maintainable systems. ITHAKA is committed to onboarding, mentorship, and continuous learning, and you will have support as you grow into new technologies and domains.

  • A minimum of 8 years as a full-stack software engineer delivering large-scale, distributed web applications.
  • Able to act as a strategic product thinker and community builder
  • Proven ability to design and develop scalable backend services and RESTful APIs.
  • Hands-on development of user-facing or internal web applications using modern frontend frameworks (e.g., React, Vue), informed by UI/UX and accessibility best practices.
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD concepts, automation, and software delivery pipelines, including tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar.
  • Practical expertise contributing to or operating internal developer platforms, enablement tooling, or shared services.
  • Strong experience working with AWS (e.g., EC2, S3, Lambda, RDS, EKS) and deploying applications using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure-as-code technologies such as Terraform.
  • Experience with event-driven architectures and messaging systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot, debug, and optimize performance across the stack.
  • Comfort collaborating in Agile, cross-functional, and distributed or self-directed teams.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate technical concepts, designs, and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Compensation & Benefits

At ITHAKA we believe in openness and equity. Part of living those values is our commitment to clarity about salary ranges, so candidates know what to expect. The starting salary for the Lead Software Engineer position ranges from $145,000 - $160,000. Starting pay may vary with job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. At present, our total compensation package for benefits-eligible employees includes medical, dental, and vision plans, an employer-paid 10% retirement contribution, paid parental and caregiver leave, 22 days of paid time off, 11 paid holidays, up to 12 sick days, wellness benefits, and more. Please note that ITHAKA, at its discretion, may make changes to its benefits programs from time to time.

Work for ITHAKA

We are committed to our organizational values of belonging, evidence, speed, teamwork, and trust. We take seriously the need for everyone to feel welcome. Belonging is one of our core values, and it shows in our vibrant culture. People from a wide range of backgrounds work at ITHAKA, and we believe that unique perspectives help us realize new insights and build better solutions.

We want to work with people who are passionate about ideas like these and who wish to contribute their perspectives and talents to ITHAKA’s mission. We enthusiastically welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and credentials. We want to hear your story and include your perspective in the transformative work we aim to do.

Learn more about Working at ITHAKA.

Apply Now

Although ITHAKA has physical offices in New York and Ann Arbor, Michigan, our employees are distributed across the continental United States. At this time, we’re not considering candidates who are unable to work and reside in the continental U.S.

Candidates may apply by submitting an application online through our career site, if you have any questions about your application, please contact us at . ITHAKA is committed to providing reasonable accommodations, if there’s anything we can do to accommodate any portion of the application or hiring process, please contact us at .

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to identity or other status protected by law. We invite you to read our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement. ITHAKA cares about your privacy, learn more about our Applicant Privacy Notice.

jobs.description:
Why ADN? Join the American Data Network family and become part of an established, purpose-driven healthcare quality organization with more than 30 years of experience. At ADN, our work supports hospitals and healthcare clients in improving quality, patient safety, and clinical outcomes. We value integrity, accuracy, collaboration, and professionalism, and we are looking for experienced abstractors who take pride in producing high-quality work.

Position Summary: American Data Network is seeking experienced NSQIP-Adult Registry Abstractors to support accurate and timely surgical registry abstraction for assigned healthcare clients. This role is ideal for candidates with recent, hands-on NSQIP-Adult abstraction experience who can independently review clinical documentation, apply registry specifications, and meet assigned deadlines with a high level of accuracy.

This is not a general data entry position. Candidates must have direct healthcare registry, clinical chart review, quality reporting, or data abstraction experience specific to NSQIP-Adult Registry.

Position Details: ADN hires both contractors and full-time employees for Data Abstraction roles. Contractors must be available for a minimum of 15 hours per week.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Reviews patient medical records and abstracts data for the NSQIP-Adult Registry.
  • Applies registry specifications, definitions, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and abstraction guidelines accurately and consistently.
  • Interprets clinical documentation related to surgical procedures, diagnoses, treatments, outcomes, complications, and related quality measures.
  • Enters accurate and complete data into assigned registry platforms, EHRs, vendor tools, or other data collection systems.
  • Maintains a high level of abstraction accuracy, completeness, and attention to detail.
  • Meets assigned productivity expectations, weekly progress goals, and internal and client deadlines.
  • Participates in quality assurance activities, including feedback, correction, validation, and IRR reviews.
  • Communicates professionally with account leads, team members, and client contacts when clarification is needed.
  • Maintains strict confidentiality and complies with ADN, client, HIPAA, and data security requirements.

Qualifications:

Required:

  • Current Surgical Clinical Reviewer certification required.
  • At least 2 years of recent NSQIP-Adult Registry abstraction experience
  • Ability to independently abstract NSQIP-Adult cases using registry specifications and clinical documentation.
  • Strong understanding of healthcare quality reporting, registry abstraction, clinical documentation review, and medical record interpretation.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, documentation, and follow-through.
  • Comfort working in multiple EHRs, registry platforms, vendor tools, and data collection systems as assigned.
  • Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills.
  • Contractors must have high-speed secure internet, a PC or laptop, and at least two monitors.

Preferred:

  • Experience using the NSQIP-Adult application, NSQIP-Adult reports, and/or other related data collection tools.
  • Experience with IRR, QA review, audit validation, and/or abstraction accuracy review.

Screening & Onboarding: Qualified candidates will complete an initial phone screen and a NSQIP-Adult specific abstraction assessment. The assessment is designed to evaluate understanding of registry specifications, abstraction judgment, accuracy, and completion speed.

ADN does not provide NSQIP-Adult abstraction training, so candidates should already have the registry experience needed for the role. After hire, ADN provides onboarding to ADN processes, client systems, EHR access, documentation tendencies, and other client-specific workflows.

Why This Role May Be a Good Fit: This position may be a strong fit for experienced NSQIP-Adult abstractors who enjoy independent work, flexible scheduling, registry-based chart review, healthcare quality reporting, and contributing to meaningful work that supports hospitals and patient care. ADN offers a knowledgeable and supportive team environment, multiple registry opportunities, and potential growth into lead or expanded quality roles for strong performers.

Role Summary

As a Civil Design Engineer II/III, you will design the site layouts, grading, drainage, and access roads that make utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage projects buildable. Civil design sets a project’s footprint on the land and shapes how it is permitted, priced, and constructed. You will turn survey, geotechnical, and site constraint data into civil land development sheet sets in AutoCAD and Civil 3D, working with structural, electrical, environmental, and project management colleagues to deliver projects that bring more renewable generation onto the grid.

As an employee-owner, you will share in the results of the work and help build a team where careful, well-documented engineering earns the trust of clients and colleagues. Candidates may be considered at either the Engineer II or Engineer III level depending on experience, technical depth, independence, and demonstrated ability to lead scope.

Core Technical & Functional Responsibilities

  • Create site layouts and civil land development sheet sets in AutoCAD and Civil 3D for utility-scale and commercial solar PV and battery energy storage projects.
  • Design site grading, earthwork, and surface drainage that balance constructability, cost, and site performance.
  • Lay out access roads, internal roads, and laydown areas that meet project and jurisdictional requirements.
  • Prepare stormwater management and erosion and sediment control plans with supporting calculations.
  • Evaluate site constraints such as topography, setbacks, wetlands, and floodplains, and develop layouts that respond to them.

Quality, Standards & Compliance

  • Document design criteria and assumptions so reviewers and clients can verify the basis of design.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Coordinate with structural, electrical, environmental, and project management staff on site layouts, equipment pads, and access.
  • Coordinate with clients, project managers, and subcontractors on project expectations and design inputs.
