jobs.excerpt: ABOUT THE ROLEAI is rewriting how every company works, and everyone is racing to figure out how to secure it.
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

AI is rewriting how every company works, and everyone is racing to figure out how to secure it. We have, and we need someone to take it to market.

The AI Security Sales Executive is a quota-carrying sales role dedicated entirely to Abnormal's AI Security suite: five products built to help customers govern AI, secure AI, and defend against rogue AI. You will own AI Security in your territory, from the first conversation through close, hunting the largest new logos while working alongside the Account Executives who already know our customers best. This is a sales role for someone who can carry a number and go as deep technically as our best engineers when a conversation demands it.

The timing matters. Abnormal is growing about 50% year over year, with more than 5,000 customers and over 30% of the Fortune 500 trusting us to protect their people. AI security now comes up in close to 80% of customer conversations at the executive level, and customers already trust our behavioral AI to solve it. Demand is outrunning capacity. You will step into a deep pipeline on day one, and you will have real say in how this category gets sold.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own AI Security in your territory. Carry the AI Security quota and run the full sales cycle end to end, from first conversation through close, including significant upsell campaigns across our existing customer base.
  • Hunt the largest new logos. Take Abnormal's AI Security story into the biggest enterprises in the world, and open doors beyond the customers who already trust us.
  • Prioritize ruthlessly. Inbound interest will outpace your calendar. Decide where your time moves the needle, and where it does not.
  • Partner with Account Executives. Work alongside the core team in your territory, equip them to carry AI Security conversations, and step in on the deals that matter most.
  • Go deep on the technology. Hold your own with security and platform teams on behavioral AI, cloud security, and agent security when a customer needs more than a standard pitch.
  • Run point on design partner conversations for products still in early availability, working closely with product leadership to shape these deals and bring the right resources to the table.
  • Shape the product and the playbook. Feed what you hear in the field back to product leadership in a fast loop, and help build how AI Security gets sold as the suite matures from early availability to GA.
  • Stay current as the suite evolves. Availability and depth will shift quickly, and you will keep pace.

WHAT YOU’LL SELL

Abnormal's AI Security suite includes five products, each at a different stage of availability:

  • AI Governance: Discovers your AI, uncovers shadow AI, and shows who's using what and at what cost.
  • AI Cloud Security: Detects and contains AI cloud breaches using behavioral AI and honeypots.
  • AI Employee Guardrails: Lets employees use AI without leaking data or triggering unintended actions.
  • AI Agent Security: Inventories an organization's AI agents and ensures they behave as intended.
  • AI Security Workbench: Lets security teams use AI to run investigations with Abnormal's models, without guardrails.

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS RIGHT NOW

Every security vendor is staking a claim in AI security. Abnormal has earned real credibility here through eight years of behavioral AI investment and a track record protecting email for thousands of customers. That trust is an advantage today, not a permanent one, and this role exists to make sure we capitalize on it while the window is open.

For the right person, that means owning a brand-new motion at the center of a fast-growing company, working directly with executive and product leadership, and building a track record as one of the people who defined how this category gets sold.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying sales experience, primarily selling into Enterprise accounts, with a proven record of winning new logos and expanding accounts.
  • Technical depth and curiosity: comfort discussing AI architecture, cloud security concepts, and how behavioral models work, in enough detail to earn trust with technical buyers.
  • A hunter's drive paired with the judgment to prioritize when demand exceeds capacity.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity. The suite and the motion for selling it are still evolving, and much of the playbook will be written by whoever takes this role on.
  • Strong cross-functional instincts. You will partner closely with Account Executives, Sales Engineering, and product leadership, and you will work autonomously between those touchpoints.

NICE TO HAVES

  • Direct experience selling AI security, cloud security, or other emerging security categories.
  • Experience in an overlay, specialist, or advisory role in cybersecurity or AI, or a record of selling into CISOs and security leaders.
  • Experience selling early-availability products and shaping design partner deals.

You’ll bring structure, visibility, and follow-through to how the team operates, leading cross-functional initiatives, creating and strengthening processes and systems, and ensuring teams have the clarity, information, and tools they need to execute effectively.

Responsibilities

Growth operational planning and performance

  • Acts as the operational driver behind strategic goals set by SVP, Growth, translating priorities into coordinated actions across campaigns, partnerships, sales initiatives, and internal workflows to ensure consistent execution and follow-through.
  • Translates growth strategy into clear, actionable plans—breaking down priorities into trackable steps, aligning stakeholders, documenting processes, and ensuring visibility into progress and next actions across teams.
  • Owns preparation and ongoing improvement of the integrated GTM dashboard, increasing visibility into activities, improving usability, and identifying opportunities to enhance it with AI and automation.
  • Owns development of recurring metrics and reporting, with support from the Growth Coordinator, ensuring data is consolidated, accurate, and aligned with growth priorities.

Sales and partnership enablement

  • Oversees pipeline hygiene and visibility, ensuring next steps are consistently updated, supporting weekly pipeline reviews, and contributing to pipeline restructuring and qualification efforts.
  • Supports sales process execution by ensuring the sales team has clear priorities, building and maintaining account planning templates and proposal submission checklists, and ensuring sales activities such as prep calls, debriefs, and follow-ups are completed with clear ownership and within defined timelines.
  • Supports new offering readiness by working with leadership to translate go-to-market plans into actionable components, including sales processes, materials, and workflows, with a focus on making them repeatable and easy for teams to execute.
  • Owns day-to-day coordination of partnership activities, including tracking next steps, maintaining partner documentation and mapping, supporting partner meetings and follow-ups, and helping identify opportunities to deepen strategic partner engagement.

Strategic initiatives and cross-functional enablement

  • Leads and project manages strategic Growth Operations initiatives, including HubSpot improvements and transformation, operationalization of the community advocacy program, and industry research and advancement initiatives, coordinating stakeholders and maintaining visibility from planning through delivery.
  • Strengthens cross-functional coordination by improving communication flows, ensuring stakeholders are informed and aligned, and helping centralize information across tools such as pipeline, partner data, and project tracking.
  • Identifies bottlenecks and creates systems to eliminate them, building repeatable processes that reduce manual effort and solve cross-functional friction.
  • Supports role clarity and capability-building across growth roles, creating playbooks, SOPs, and templates to harmonize workflows so teams can collaborate more effectively.
  • Facilitates growth team huddles, cross-team forums, and retrospectives.
  • Manages vendor relationships where applicable.

Professional Development

  • Own your growth by setting and updating development goals, actively seeking feedback, and aligning your aspirations with business goals.
  • Contribute to internal initiatives that impact the client and/or team member experience such as our Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Advisory Committee, Community Impact Committee, or our Social Committee.
  • Bring forward smarter, faster, better solutions to processes and identify opportunities to be more agile in day-to-day activities.
  • Demonstrate inclusive and supportive behavior, contributing to BrandActive’s core values of trust, agility, and growth, commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion, (EDI), humanity, and wellbeing.

Qualifications and Experience

This role is for someone who thinks about Growth Operations holistically—how an integrated sales and marketing team works together, how priorities move across functions, and how the right processes, systems, information, and operating rhythms enable the team to perform. It is not a traditional Marketing Operations or technology-focused role; while tools such as HubSpot and project management platforms are important enablers, the focus is on improving how the broader Growth team operates.

You might not tick every box, but if you meet most of the qualifications and are excited about the role, we’d love to hear from you. We value potential, curiosity, and a growth mindset.

  • Strong project and program management skills, with experience translating strategic priorities into structured plans and coordinating multiple workstreams through execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, align stakeholders, and drive clear ownership, decisions, and follow-through.
  • Strong ability to manage up by anticipating needs, proactively surfacing risks and decisions, and providing leadership with clear visibility into progress and priorities.
  • Experience shaping and improving project management systems, processes, and ways of working to increase team effectiveness and reduce friction.
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to lead productive meetings and working sessions across teams and levels of seniority.
  • Highly organized and process-minded, with strong judgment, initiative, and the ability to identify roadblocks and bring forward practical solutions.
  • Strong analytical and reporting skills, with the ability to consolidate information, identify meaningful insights, and support data-informed decision-making.
  • Comfortable working across CRM, reporting, project management, and collaboration platforms; experience with HubSpot and using automation or AI to improve workflows is critical.

Compensation and Benefits

BrandActive offers a comprehensive compensation and benefits package, including:

  • Parental leave benefits to support you and your family.
  • $2,000 annual professional and personal development support, including funding and time off for learning to support your growth.

  • Flexible work options – Remote (open to BC, Alberta, Ontario provinces) with adaptable schedules.
  • Two annual town halls in Toronto, featuring engaging sessions and fun team activities.
  • Supportive leadership and career development, with ongoing coaching and feedback to help you grow and succeed, quarterly formal feedback, annual performance reviews and separate annual development meetings.
  • Work-from-anywhere flexibility, with the option to work abroad for up to four weeks (in eligible countries and after a minimum tenure depending on the role and circumstance).
  • And more!

Immediately

jobs.description:
About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is seeking a People Systems, Analytics and AI Manager to be our subject matter expert on HR systems and to turn People data into insights that help business leaders make better decisions. You will build the reports, analytics, and dashboards that tell the story of our workforce, and you will use AI tooling to make those stories faster to create, easier to understand, and more compelling.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director, People Programs, Systems and Analytics. You will work closely with People Operations, Finance, and leaders across the business, and you will own your work from question to insight to action.

We are looking for someone who combines deep HR systems knowledge with strong analytical skills, creativity in how data is presented, and sound judgment about people data and AI.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the subject matter expert for our HR systems (HRIS, applicant tracking, performance, compensation, and learning platforms), including configuration, data integrity, security roles, integrations, and release management.
  • Design, build, and maintain reports, dashboards, and analytics on headcount, hiring, retention, engagement, compensation, and workforce planning that leaders use to make decisions.
  • Partner with People, Finance, and business leaders to translate questions into clear metrics, definitions, and analyses, and to recommend actions based on what the data shows.
  • Use AI tools to accelerate analysis and create compelling data stories and visualizations, including automated insights, natural-language summaries, and executive-ready narratives.
  • Establish and govern People data standards: metric definitions, data quality checks, documentation, and a single source of truth across systems.
  • Protect employee data by applying privacy, confidentiality, and access controls, and by partnering with Legal and Security on responsible use of AI with People data.
  • Own the intake, prioritization, and delivery of system and reporting requests, balancing quick turnarounds with scalable, self-service solutions.
  • Automate recurring reports and manual workflows to reduce effort and errors, and identify new opportunities where systems and AI can improve the employee and manager experience.
  • Support system projects such as new module rollouts, integrations, data migrations, and annual cycles (performance, compensation, and engagement), including testing, training, and documentation.
  • Enable People Operations teammates and managers through training, office hours, and clear guides so they can use data and tools with confidence.
  • Stay current on HR technology, analytics, and AI trends, and bring practical recommendations to the Director, People Programs, Systems and Analytics.

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of related experience in HR systems, People analytics, or HR operations, with hands-on ownership of reporting and dashboards in a technology or high-growth environment.
  • Expert-level knowledge of at least one major HRIS (for example, Workday, Rippling, or similar), including report writing, calculated fields, and security configuration.
  • Strong proficiency with analytics and visualization tools (for example, SQL, Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar) and advanced spreadsheet skills.
  • Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling to analyze data, generate insights, and build visualizations and narratives, with sound judgment about accuracy and appropriate use.
  • Ability to translate business questions into metrics and communicate findings clearly to non-technical leaders.
  • Strong understanding of data integrity, privacy, and confidentiality practices for employee data.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects and stakeholders independently and deliver on time with attention to detail.
  • Curious, pragmatic problem solver who enjoys simplifying complex processes and data.
  • Comfortable working with a highly distributed team across time zones.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with data pipelines, data warehouses, or scripting (for example, Python or dbt).
  • Experience with integrations and workflow automation tools.
  • Knowledge of workforce planning, compensation, or engagement analytics.
  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Analytics, Business, Human Resources, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $121,800 - $167,530**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $109,700 - $150,810**

jobs.description:
About Improvado

Improvado is an AI-powered marketing data platform built for mid-market and enterprise teams. We help companies automate complex marketing data workflows, unify data at scale, and surface insights through BI and AI. Brands like Genentech, T-Mobile, Activision, and H&R Block rely on us to simplify analytics and improve marketing performance.

We’re a fast-growing Series A startup backed by $34M in funding and driven by a team that moves fast, stays curious, and cares about high-quality execution.

About the role

Improvado is a marketing data platform for enterprise brands and agencies. You will own how our revenue runs and how it is measured. That covers Salesforce and the GTM tools, the path from signed contract to paid invoice, the revenue data model, and the reports leadership decides from. You work closely with the analytics team: you don’t have to build the data models yourself, but you must read them, spot what is wrong and say what to change. You work through AI agents daily, doing the work of a bigger team.

What you will do

Salesforce and GTM stack

  • Own Salesforce configuration, release process and user access, plus the integrations around it (Gong, Clay, Lemlist, enrichment, e-signature, lead routing).
  • Keep CRM data clean with guardrails that block mistakes. Manage licences and vendor renewals.
  • Maintain the Salesforce manual and RevOps SOPs, and train new hires.

Contract to cash

  • Own ARR and bookings logic (new, upsell, downsell, churn, renewals) and keep agreement, opportunity, and invoice consistent.
  • Run the closed-deals and billing check with Finance. Fix errors at the source and add a control so they don’t repeat.
  • Audit invoices, track and chase unpaid ones, and prepare quarterly commission and quota reports.

Revenue analytics and data model

  • Own the quarterly sales analytics pack, the CRO report, the forecast and pipeline coverage (including CS renewal inputs).
  • Track funnel conversion, explain why deals move, stall or slip, and keep attribution correct with Marketing.
  • Query ClickHouse daily, trace any number to its source, and write specs for model changes. Give each metric one documented definition and add data quality checks.
  • Build leadership dashboards, retire unused ones, and end every analysis with a recommendation, a number and an owner.

AI and automation

  • Use coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) for queries, scripts and Salesforce automation, and always verify their output.
  • Automate manual work (invoice and payment checks, CRM hygiene, deal-risk alerts, call analysis) and measure hours saved and errors avoided.

Ownership

  • Be the single RevOps contact for Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance and Product. Turn each request into a task with an owner, date and success metric.

Requirements

  • 4-6+ years in RevOps, Sales Ops or GTM systems in B2B SaaS, with hands-on admin of a live Salesforce org.
  • Strong SQL and comfort in a modeled warehouse (layers, lineage, one definition per metric). dbt is a plus.
  • Deep knowledge of the B2B SaaS revenue cycle: funnel, pipeline, forecast, ARR, churn, renewals.

The Senior Accounting Manager plays a key leadership role within Annie’s finance organization and serves as a strategic partner to the SVP of Finance. Financial Close & Reporting

Revenue, Cost of Services & Inventory Accounting (GAAP)

Acquisition Accounting & Integration Support

Team Partnership & Execution

Controls, Audit & Process Improvement

  • Support a strong internal control environment through review standards, documentation, and segregation of duties

  • Identify opportunities to improve close efficiency, reduce manual risk, and enhance reporting quality
  • Partner on system implementations and process standardization initiatives, including NetSuite enhancements

Qualifications

  • Active CPA required
  • 7+ years of progressive accounting experience
  • Strong experience in multi-entity or multi-location accounting and reporting
  • Familiarity working in NetSuite
  • Strong understanding of GAAP, internal controls, and audit requirements

jobs.description:
¿Qué es?

Es un ingeniero especializado en el diseño, desarrollo y liberación de arneses de alta tensión (HV) y baja tensión (LV) para vehículos eléctricos o sistemas automotrices. Su rol es clave para garantizar que los arneses cumplan con los estándares de seguridad, calidad y manufacturabilidad, además de servir como enlace técnico entre el equipo de ingeniería y los fabricantes.

¿Cómo lo hace?

Diseña y documenta arneses utilizando herramientas como Siemens Capital Essentials (para dibujos 2D) y CATIA (para modelos 3D), asegurando que los diseños sean precisos y compatibles con los esquemas eléctricos y físicos definidos.

Mantiene librerías de componentes en Capital Essentials, incluyendo conectores, terminales, sellos y accesorios, para garantizar la selección automática de piezas compatibles.

Colabora con fabricantes (especialmente en China) para resolver problemas técnicos, gestionar cambios de ingeniería (ECRs) y soportar procesos como APQP/PPAP.

Apoya la producción en sitio, identificando y documentando problemas de calidad, instalación o servicio, y proponiendo mejoras para la manufactura masiva.

Asegura el cumplimiento de normativas y estándares como USCAR-37, IEC 60664-1, ISO 6469-3 e IPC/WHMA-A-620, críticos para sistemas de alta tensión.

¿Por qué es importante?

Su trabajo es esencial para garantizar que los arneses HV/LV sean seguros, funcionales y listos para producción, evitando fallas en etapas avanzadas del desarrollo. Además, su capacidad para comunicarse en inglés y chino mandarín facilita la coordinación con equipos globales y fabricantes, asegurando que los proyectos avancen sin retrasos.

Siemens Capital Essentials (creación de dibujos 2D de manufactura para arneses) – Nivel avanzado (+5 años de experiencia).

Diseño de arneses HV/LV (selección de componentes, ruteo, y consideraciones de manufacturabilidad) – Nivel intermedio (2-5 años de experiencia).

Conocimiento de sistemas de alta tensión (HV):Busbars, fusibles, conectores HV, cables blindados/orange, HVIL – Nivel intermedio (2-5 años de experiencia).

Normativas y estándares:USCAR-37 (sistemas de conexión HV) – Nivel intermedio (2-5 años de experiencia).

IEC 60664-1 (creepage/clearance) – Nivel intermedio (2-5 años de experiencia).

ISO 6469-3 (seguridad eléctrica en EVs) – Nivel básico (0-2 años de experiencia).

Procesos de calidad:APQP/PPAP – Nivel intermedio (2-5 años de experiencia).

Engineering Change Requests (ECRs) – Nivel intermedio (2-5 años de experiencia).

jobs.description:
Embed with the platform and engineering teams who adopt Earthly Lunar, get them live in production, and turn their hardest standards into enforced guardrails — writing real code the whole way.

About Earthly Lunar

Earthly Lunar is a guardrails engine for the AI era. As engineering organizations scale — and AI accelerates how much code they ship — leaders lose the ability to hold every team to their standards for quality, security, and compliance. Lunar turns those standards into automated guardrails enforced across the whole software development lifecycle — as code is written, on every pull request, and at deploy — consistently across every repo and team. Engineering leaders get back control and real-time visibility, and compliance evidence becomes a byproduct of enforcement. Whether code comes from a developer or an AI agent, Lunar makes sure it ships right.

We're an AI-native team backed by Innovation Endeavors and Work-Bench — with angels including Jeff Dean (Google's Chief Scientist), the CEOs of Datadog and Cockroach Labs, the founder of Sentry, and the creators of Elixir, Pandas, and Ruff/uv. We're trusted by enterprise teams across defense and large-scale SaaS, and growing fast.

The role

You're a hard-core engineer who happens to love working with customers. You'll work with the platform and engineering teams evaluating and adopting Lunar — before and after the sale — and own their success end to end: prove the fit, guide the deployment into their environment, then build alongside them to turn their real-world standards into automated, enforced guardrails. You own technical delivery for each account, from first call to guardrails running in production.

Lunar is a deeply technical product. Getting it deployed means Kubernetes, Helm, CI/CD, and a GitHub App; getting value from it means writing collectors and policies — small programs (Bash/Python) that gather signals from across a customer's SDLC (Dockerfiles, K8s manifests, Terraform, SBOMs, CI runs, VCS and vendor APIs) and evaluate them against the customer's standards. That's the same work our library, lunar-lib, is built from — and you'll own and extend it. The patterns you build in the field flow back into the product, so every customer benefits from the last.

This is a hands-on engineering role: you write and own production code, and success looks like a customer's custom guardrails live and enforcing across thousands of engineers within ~90 days.

What you'll do

  • Own each account's technical track end to end. From the technical evaluation before the deal closes, through install and first guardrails live, to expansion and long-term success — the whole arc is yours.

  • Be the technical partner in the sale. Be the credible engineer in the room before the deal closes — scope the fit, prove the value on the customer's real stack, and field the hardest technical questions.

  • Guide the install, hands-on. Stand up the self-hosted Lunar Hub with the customer's team — Helm chart on Kubernetes, Postgres, S3, the GitHub App, the CI agent, and Grafana dashboards — and debug it live when their environment throws you a curveball.

  • Turn standards into guardrails. Sit with a platform team, understand a real requirement — a post-incident action item, a compliance rule, an org convention — and write the collector and policy that enforces it across all their repos and pipelines.

  • Write production code daily. Bash, Python, SQL — parsing Dockerfiles and K8s manifests, wiring up GitHub/GitLab and vendor APIs, normalizing messy signals into clean posture data.

  • Feed the product. Generalize what you build with customers into lunar-lib so it ships to everyone.

  • Own the fix. When a deployment breaks, you diagnose and resolve it yourself rather than filing a ticket — often with the customer's team watching.

  • Own the relationship for the long haul. Earn the trust of platform and engineering leaders and the ICs on their teams, keep them successful and expanding long after go-live, and translate between their world and ours.

  • Build with AI, and build the AI story. Use Claude Code, Codex or any other AI tools extensively. Unlimited tokens available.

What we're looking for

These are the must-haves. The first three are non-negotiable.

  • MUST: AI-native to the core. The majority of your work is AI-assisted. You build with Claude Code / agents every day, you build your own AI workflows, and you're pushing the frontier of how one engineer does the work of a team. If you're not already living this way, this isn't the role for you.

  • MUST: You genuinely love customers. You'd rather be in the room untangling a customer's gnarliest deployment than heads-down in isolation. You're calm and credible in front of platform and engineering leaders, and you get energy from making them successful.

  • MUST: Both a builder AND an ops person. You write real production code and you're at home in the platform/infra world. Ops alone isn't enough — we need you fluent writing code. Dev alone isn't enough — we need real ops instincts. You have to be both.

  • Real platform / SRE / DevOps chops. Expert with Dockerfiles. Comfortable enough with Kubernetes to guide a live Helm-chart install and debug it. Fluent across multiple CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Buildkite, CircleCI, Jenkins, and friends).

  • Mid-level, with a strong aptitude for growth. We weight the ability to learn quickly and take initiative over a complete match against every requirement listed here. A solid platform background that's less developed in some areas is fine, provided you are deeply curious to learn fast.

  • High ownership. You navigate ambiguity, set your own path, and own outcomes without waiting to be told how.

  • Backgrounds we love: ex-founders (a failed startup is a plus, not a red flag), technical ex-consultants, and early stage engineers who've shipped B2B products hand-in-hand with customers.

Nice to have

Bring any of these and we'll be glad. Nobody has all of them.

  • Languages: Bash, Python, Go, SQL, TypeScript/Node, Earthfiles.

  • Kubernetes & delivery: authoring Helm charts (not just installing them), ArgoCD, k8s RBAC / NetworkPolicies / ingress.

  • Infrastructure as code: Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi (and comfort reading HCL).

  • Observability: Grafana, OpenTelemetry / OTLP, Prometheus, Datadog.

  • APIs everywhere: GitHub / GitLab APIs, and wiring up the APIs of dev-infra and production-infra tools in general (PagerDuty, Jira/Linear, container registries, cloud providers).

  • Supply chain & code analysis: SBOMs (Syft, Trivy, cdxgen), SCA/SAST (Snyk, Semgrep, Gitleaks), signing & provenance (cosign, SLSA), OPA/Rego, ast-grep / tree-sitter.

  • AI-native building: MCP servers, agent skills and sub-agents, editor/agent hooks (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex).

  • Config wrangling: parsing YAML, HCL, JSON, Dockerfiles, CODEOWNERS into clean structured data.

  • Startup DNA: startup experience; a failed-founder background is a big bonus; a desire to start your own thing one day is very welcome.

  • Product sense: B2B product-building experience, working directly with the customer.

  • Regulated / defense context: familiarity with SOC 2, NIST SSDF, FedRAMP, CMMC, or PCI DSS (some of our customers are in defense and finance).

  • The adjacent space: developer portals / internal platforms (Backstage, Cortex, OpsLevel).

You might not be a fit if

  • You'd rather stay heads-down and away from customers.

  • You want a pure sales-engineering or solutions-architect role and don't really want to write production code — there's plenty of customer-facing work here, but the core bar is that you can build.

  • You're an infra operator who doesn't want to write code — or a developer who doesn't want to touch infra.

  • You need every requirement fully spec'd before you start; this role is high-ambiguity by design.

How we work

  • Small, senior, AI-native team. Heavy AI leverage, high autonomy, fast loops.

  • Your field work becomes the product. What you build with customers lands in lunar-lib and ships to everyone.

  • Top-down go-to-market. We win platform and engineering leaders; you help win them over technically, then make them wildly successful.

  • Direct line to the founder/CEO and outsized ownership of how Lunar lands in the real world.

Compensation & logistics

  • Base salary: $160,000–$210,000 (US base), depending on experience — plus equity.

  • Location: Remote (US & Canada).

  • Travel: Occasional — customer onsites and team gatherings, at most one trip per quarter.

  • Type: Full-time.

Benefits

  • Healthcare, dental, and vision — including dependents (US & Canada)

  • Incentive stock plan

  • 401(k) / RRSP with employer matching (US & Canada)

  • Life insurance (US & Canada)

  • Credits for gym or activity equipment (US & Canada)

  • Fully remote, with everyone within ±3 hours of each other — no late-night meetings

  • An early-stage environment where your work has outsized impact and you operate with real freedom — excellent preparation if you want to take the founder path someday

The salary range above is the US base salary for this full-time position. It does not include equity, bonuses, or other benefits. Ranges are determined by role, level, and location; within the range, individual pay reflects job-related skills, experience, and training. We expect to hire near the middle of the range, and would pay near the top only in rare cases where a candidate's experience far exceeds what the role requires. Your hiring contact can share specifics for your location during the process.

Salary: 160K - 210K USD a year

We are looking for an outcome-oriented, commercially minded Delivery Manager to run the execution and scaling of our patient services hub platforms. You will own the answer to one question: is it going to ship when we said it would? Releases, features, integrations, and fixes - on time, at quality, in a compliance-heavy environment where a missed date has a downstream cost to patients waiting on therapy.

This is the operational engine of our technology organization. You will be the connective tissue between the Product Owner, who decides what gets built, and the developers who build it - while keeping work synchronized with our AI Lead, data team, and IT operations group. Externally, you are the delivery counterpart to our Implementation leaders.

We expect you to work with AI, not around it. The team runs on Jira, Confluence, and Rovo and uses Claude and Claude Code in its daily practice. We want less manual ticket maintenance and status assembly and more forward-looking signal - earlier risk detection, better forecasting, dependencies surfaced before they reach a developer. You will help build that capability rather than inherit it finished.

Status reporting exists to provide transparency into where things stand, not to fill a meeting. The same applies to process: we want agile practice tailored to a fast-moving, highly regulated healthcare business rather than a framework followed by the book. All of it in service of our mission to remove barriers between patients and the care they need.

Core Duties/Responsibilities:

  • On-Time Delivery: Own delivery predictability and execution against commitments. Plan, sequence, and drive sprint and release execution so that features, enhancements, integrations, and fixes land when promised - and when a date is at risk, surface it early with options rather than late with an explanation.
  • Delivery Flow & Execution Discipline: Actively manage work from sprint commitment through completion. Maintain visibility to work in progress, aging items, blockers, handoffs, carry-over, and unplanned work; intervene early when execution drifts. Establish and reinforce clear ownership, estimation, status, and definition-of-done practices so work does not stall silently or move outside the delivery process.
  • Release and Environment Coordination: Own release planning and readiness across development, sandbox, UAT, and production, ensuring required approvals, deployment plans, rollback plans, environment readiness, and post-deployment verification are coordinated and completed.
  • Cross-Functional Dependency Management: Map, manage, and unblock dependencies across the Product Owner, development team, AI Lead, data team, IT Ops, and external integrations. Work ahead of the team to surface technical and operational dependencies early, sequence shared work deliberately, and prevent dependencies from colliding mid-sprint or threatening delivery commitments.
  • Vendor and Partner Coordination: Serve as the technical and delivery counterpart to Implementation in engagements with pharma brand partners, specialty pharmacies, and data vendors - tracking third-party commitments, integration readiness, and the external dependencies that affect our dates.
  • Capacity and Contract Resourcing: Forecast team capacity against committed and anticipated demand, accounting for PTO, production support, unplanned work, dependencies, and competing initiatives. Partner with the Product Owner to establish realistic sprint and release commitments. Decide when to augment with contract resources, then own their onboarding, workload, throughput, and quality - and the utilization data behind staffing and budget decisions.
  • AI-Assisted Delivery Operations: Use Jira, Confluence, Rovo, Claude, and Claude Code to reduce manual tracking and reporting effort and to strengthen risk visibility, forecasting accuracy, and early blocker detection across the delivery pipeline.
  • Compliance-Gated Execution: Ensure deployment schedules, data flows, and platform changes align with HIPAA, TCPA, OIG guidance, and organizational change management and security policy - with traceable records of work, approvals, and deployments.
  • Transparent Delivery Reporting: Report in plain language on progress, release timing, risk, and trade-offs, and track the measures that show whether delivery is actually improving: on-time release rate, cycle and lead time, carry-over, unplanned work, and escaped defects.
  • Pragmatic Agile Leadership: Facilitate planning, refinement, stand-ups, reviews, and retrospectives in whatever form serves the work. Coach the team on breakdown, estimation, and definition-of-done discipline, protect focus from mid-sprint churn, and turn retrospective findings into changes that stick.

¿Qué es?

Es un ingeniero especializado en el diseño mecánico de estructuras para aplicaciones industriales, específicamente en el sector automotriz y de vehículos eléctricos. Su enfoque principal es desarrollar componentes estructurales críticos, como carcasas de baterías, estructuras de montaje y ensambles electromecánicos, asegurando que cumplan con los estándares de calidad, fabricabilidad y funcionalidad.

¿Cómo lo hace?

Utiliza herramientas de diseño 3D (CATIA V5/V6) para crear modelos detallados y dibujos técnicos con tolerancias geométricas (GD&T).

Colabora con equipos multidisciplinarios (eléctricos, térmicos, de control) para garantizar la integración perfecta de los componentes mecánicos con otros sistemas.

Aplica su conocimiento en procesos de fabricación (hojalatería, maquinado, soldadura) para optimizar el diseño y facilitar la producción.

Actúa como enlace técnico entre el equipo de ingeniería y los proveedores, coordinando requisitos, plazos y resolución de problemas.

Valida los diseños mediante simulaciones y pruebas físicas, asegurando que los componentes cumplan con las especificaciones técnicas y normativas (ej: ASME Y14.5, ISO 2768).

¿Por qué es importante?

Su trabajo es clave para el desarrollo de vehículos eléctricos y sistemas de transporte pesado, ya que garantiza que las estructuras mecánicas sean seguras, eficientes y fabricables. Además, su capacidad para comunicarse efectivamente con equipos globales (especialmente en Asia) asegura que los proyectos avancen sin retrasos y con alta precisión técnica.

Requirements

Habilidades Específicas

  • Dominio de CATIA V5/V6 para diseño 3D y creación de dibujos 2D con GD&T (ASME Y14.5 o GB/T).
  • Experiencia en diseño de estructuras para vehículos eléctricos o OEMs automotrices.
  • Conocimiento de procesos de fabricación y su impacto en el diseño (ej: tolerancias, materiales).
  • Capacidad para liderar la comunicación con proveedores (alinear requisitos técnicos, plazos y resolución de problemas).

Habilidades Deseables

  • Experiencia en sistemas de alto voltaje (HV) y pruebas de validación automotriz.
  • Conocimiento de estándares mecánicos/automotrices (ISO 1101, VDI 2230, ISO 6469).
  • Habilidad para interpretar diagramas eléctricos y realizar análisis de apilamiento de tolerancias (RSS Statistical Analysis).
  • Soft Skills: Proactivo, organizado, orientado al detalle y con excelentes habilidades de comunicación intercultural.

jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for an Environmental Policy & Compliance Analyst to join our environmental compliance team.

Position Description

The Environmental Policy & Compliance Analyst is responsible for analyzing the resource areas included in a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) report. This includes performing research and technical analyses for resource areas such as, but not limited to, land use, water resources, air resources, and socioeconomics. The Analyst position is responsible for documentation of each of the resource areas in environmental deliverables to the lead agency performing the NEPA analysis. This position also supports providing technical work for State and local compliance requirements as needed.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Research, analyze, and interpret Federal environmental laws, regulations, and guidance
  • Evaluate the policy implications of proposed legislation, regulations, and agency actions
  • Draft and revise Environmental Reports for NEPA and briefing materials
  • Support development of internal environmental technical processes and compliance frameworks
  • Track regulatory changes and assess risk, compliance gaps, and operational impacts
  • Assist with environmental permitting processes (air, water, waste, land use, etc.)
  • Support compliance with NEPA, NHPA, Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and the Endangered Species Act
  • Interface with regulatory agencies (e.g., NRC, DOE) to clarify requirements and respond to inquiries
  • Review technical studies and consultant reports for accuracy and policy alignment
  • Incorporate technical studies into NEPA documentation
  • Prepare materials and lead meetings with regulators
  • Maintain organized records of regulatory correspondence
  • Monitor emerging trends in environmental policy
  • Support audits, inspections, and internal reviews as needed

Experience Level:

  • Intermediate (2-5yr) or Experienced (5-10yr)

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s, Master’s or Ph.D in Environmental Policy, Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Natural Resources, Public Policy, Sustainability, or a closely related field or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience in NEPA compliance with the NRC or DOE
  • Experience in Ohio, Tennessee, Idaho, Alaska

Competencies

We are looking for an Environmental Policy & Compliance Analyst that:

  • Has a working knowledge of environmental laws and regulations (Federal, State, and local)
  • Is able to interpret statutes, rules, permits, and guidance documents and assess complex regulatory requirements
  • Is able to evaluate likelihood and severity of different regulatory strategies
  • Understands NRC and DOE regulatory processes and agency roles
  • Aware of how policy changes affect compliance obligations and operations
  • Familiar with NEPA documentation
  • Is able to analyze environmental and compliance data
  • Is able to review and evaluate technical studies and consultant reports
  • Is able to write clear, accurate technical and regulatory documents
  • Communicate effectively with regulators, consultants, and internal stakeholders
  • Is able to manage multiple priorities
  • Detail oriented and able to spot inconsistencies or errors in compliance materials
  • Motivated to stay current on evolving regulations and policy trends
  • Open to feedback and skill development
  • Passionate about clean energy
  • An optimist at heart
  • Passionate about making advanced fission a reality
  • Willing and able to learn quickly
  • Willing to think differently and do things in new ways
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment
  • Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving while not leaning only on what has been done before
  • Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems
  • An excellent writer who can write in a modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well!
  • Able to communicate technical content and results verbally

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

About Oklo compensation: $100,000-$150,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, competitive pay, 401k, health insurance, FSA, flexible work hours, and other benefits.

We are looking to fill this position immediately!

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Customer Success team within Signature Success is looking for a driven and customer-focused Customer Success Manager (CSM) to serve as a primary contact point for Salesforce’s largest and highest-profile customers. You will have responsibility for partnering with a small number of assigned accounts, maintaining a continual focus on the customer’s business goals to improve their overall technical and operational health and realize the maximum value out of their Salesforce investment. The Customer Success Manager maintains awareness of the customer's key events, needs, potential risks, and value drivers.

As a trusted advisor, the CSM will build a track record in customer success through superb communication with partners and extensive knowledge of the Salesforce platform to translate their business needs to solutions. You will forge relationships with your customers and account teams, develop a deep technical understanding of their Salesforce implementation, share standard methodologies, and adoption of proactive services. These activities will enable you to proactively set the customer up for success through optimization of the platform, with special care during critically important peak events.

As a CSM, you will occasionally act as a point of contact for any major incidents, owning the customer’s expectations and communications through the resolution of such incidents. The CSM acts as the technical main interface on behalf of our customers and works closely across both internal and external collaborators, including partners and ISVs, as required to address the customer needs.

The ideal CSM has an extraordinary focus on the success of the customer, is an exceptional communicator, exhibits professionalism, is dedicated to meeting and exceeding expectations, enjoys forming relationships, has excellent collaboration skills, and has the ability to learn new technologies quickly.

Your Impact

  • Function as the Core Cloud Subject Matter Expert (SME) for the technical and operational configuration (and needs) of the customer.
  • Serve as the single point of customer accountability responsible for orchestration of all Signature deliverables, experience, and renewal, and expansion.
  • Cultivate and maintain stakeholder relationships with the customer’s IT and business executive leadership, sponsors, and decision-makers within customer organizations that have purchased Signature.
  • Help your customers achieve their business goals and outcomes on the Salesforce Marketing platform by:
  • Coordinating the completion of the Signature Success catalog of services as required for your customer
  • Providing timely, proactive Salesforce feature guidance based on the areas of interest for your customer
  • Acting as an advisor to your customers for the adoption of new features of Salesforce’s annual release schedules and identifying potential challenges and risks to your customer's implementation
  • Communicate the value of Signature Success. Be accountable for ensuring all collaborators understand this value so that customers continue to renew Signature Success.
  • Act as an advocate for customers during the triage and resolution of high severity cases to assist with the timely resolution of these issues.
  • Proactive Support & Enhancement: Conduct quarterly reviews, identify trends, and provide tailored release recommendations to ensure stability, performance, and feature enhancement.
  • Internal Relationship Building: Forge strong multidisciplinary relationships with Sales, Engineering, and Product Management to lead and coordinate customer relationships for success and revenue opportunities.
  • The CSM may be required to occasionally be available for some after-hour or weekend coverage depending on the customer’s need.
  • Evolution of Roles: Anticipate and adapt to role changes per evolving Salesforce needs.

Minimum Skills:

  • Experienced professional with 5+ years of relevant industry expertise in Technical Customer Success, Customer Success Manager, SaaS platform use or project leadership, Technology Consulting, Technology Solutions Development, Technical and/or Solutions Architecture.
  • Exceptional communication and presentation skills with demonstrated ability to communicate and influence effectively at all levels of the organization, including executive and C-level.
  • Skills for both analyzing technical concepts and translating them into business terms and for mapping business requirements into technical features.
  • Ability to explain complex technical concepts in business-friendly terms to customers, then explain customer needs to internal partners.
  • Coordinate and work closely with high volume events and/or key events for the customer.
  • Experience leading efforts of cross-functional teams to facilitate resolution or disposition of customer needs or projects.

Preferred Requirements:

  • +2 years in Salesforce Ecosystem.
  • Salesforce product certifications are a plus
  • Knowledge of Salesforce Core Cloud features and applications and able to articulate the value and how a Customer can benefit from Signature Success
  • Knowledge of Salesforce product suite and features, capabilities, best use, and how to deploy, including knowledge of the Salesforce platform and ecosystem.
  • Degree or equivalent experience required. Experience will be evaluated based on the strengths you'll need for the role (e.g. demonstrated behaviors in previous jobs, that align to role needs such as extracurricular leadership roles, military experience, volunteer roles, work experience

jobs.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

JOB SUMMARY


The objective is to support on-time delivery of products at the best possible price while minimizing production inventory levels for Avid and its suppliers. This role is responsible for and manages purchasing, materials requirements planning, inventory levels, supplier performance, and ERP data maintenance throughout the production life cycle.


RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

  • Cross functional and cross company partnership with product quality, order fulfillment, manufacturing engineering, sourcing, new product introduction, and logistics teams to support customer success.
  • Focus on delivering against specific metrics aimed at on-time delivery, approved cost, availability, and on-time shipment.
  • Manages supplier and supply chain vendors to execute strategic material programs, yield minimum excess and obsolete inventory, and minimize material shortages.
  • Functional understanding of material requirements planning to judge the accuracy of and need to act upon purchase requisitions.
  • Approval and execution of engineering change orders or deviations impacting material availability, material obsolescence, and production throughput.
  • Supporting the entirety of product manufacturing life cycles with concentrated effort applied to introduction, growth, and phase out. Includes calculating and executing last time buy purchases followed by stock depletion.
  • Understanding supplier contracts and KPI’s to support supplier performance and protect Avid from undue inventory liability.
  • Partnering with sourcing to optimize supplier selections.
  • ERP data maintenance including but not limited to purchase info. records, source lists, buyer codes, lead-times, MOQ‘s, ROP’s, and safety stocks.
  • Prompt resolution of invoice discrepancies with accounts payable to allow on time payment.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

  • Bachelor’s degree in business/supply chain or Industrial Engineering preferred.
  • 1-2 years of professional experience in supply chain procurement, planning, or sourcing desired.
  • Experience purchasing electro-mechanical assemblies with PCBA content is preferred.
  • Experience using NetSuite or equivalent ERP database systems.
  • Experience in lean manufacturing, supply chain, and inventory stocking strategies preferred.
  • Experience using Third Party Logistics for finished goods storage and distribution.
  • Ability to understand inventory impact on cash flow, costing activities, and price negotiation.
  • Must have a demonstrated ability to set and achieve goals and meet objectives.
  • Requires strong Microsoft office computer skills with the ability to provide management updates, oral and written presentations, supplier status summary, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience using Artificial Intelligence to solve problems and gain efficiency preferred.

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

jobs.description:
Head of Analytics — Global Multi-Product Broker

Limassol, Cyprus (or remote within UTC–1 to UTC+4) · Reports to CMO · Greenfield function build

The company has scaled across CFDs, crypto, prop trading, and prediction markets without end-to-end analytics — and the person who walks in now gets to define what data-driven decision-making means there, permanently.

Most analytics leadership roles hand you someone else's stack, someone else's definitions, and someone else's hiring mistakes. This one doesn't. The company has no existing analytics function, no inherited architecture, and no canonical data model. It also has no prior Head of Analytics, which means no prior culture to unpick, no legacy tooling to defend, and no one else's choices to work around. The architectural decisions made here — attribution model, data stack, canonical metric definitions, testing methodology — are not modifications to someone else's framework. They are the decisions.

The mandate starts with acquisition attribution. The CMO needs to answer, for any campaign across any channel, what it cost, what it produced, and what those traders did next. That foundation — unified tracking from first click to live trading activity, across paid search, paid social, affiliates, mobile, and partner codes — is the condition that makes everything else possible. From there: a single source of truth for business-critical metrics, real-time KPIs across every major product, and a hypothesis-testing framework that gets teams running experiments instead of debating whether to. Prediction markets are on the horizon; this person arrives at exactly the moment data moves from nice-to-have to genuine competitive advantage.

This is not a role for someone who needs a running start. The first months require building from zero — infrastructure, tooling, practices — in an organisation that has operated successfully without them. That sentence should produce recognition, not hesitation.

Why this beats the seat you're in now

  • Blank page, real authority. Unilateral control over data definitions, roadmap prioritisation, and build sequencing. The CMO is the escalation point for cross-functional conflicts — not a co-decider on routine calls.
  • Your name on the foundation. The stack, the canonical model, the attribution methodology, the team culture — all of it takes the shape you give it, and stays that way. No one who spent five years maintaining an inherited instance can tell this story.
  • Performance upside tied to impact, not discretion. The bonus is structured as a share of the incremental value this function generates — not a manager's year-end judgment call.
  • Team built your way. There is no inherited team to manage around. Embedded analysts exist and will be directed by this role; longer-term hiring is a blank page you fill with culture first.
  • Inflection-point timing. New products, new markets — the window where data definitions and infrastructure choices become permanent is open right now, not in two years.
  • Breadth that consulting can't give you. You design the architecture and then watch it run at scale, own the outcome, and make the hiring decisions. The exit story is yours.

This is for you if

  • You have built multi-touch attribution across paid, organic, and partner channels in a fintech or fast-moving digital business — and you have made a contested attribution model stick with channel owners who didn't want it to.
  • You have made a defensible architecture call from a blank page — not just inherited and maintained someone else's stack.
  • You currently hold a senior analytics role at a CFD, crypto, or adjacent broker and you are waiting for a function-head opening that may not come, or may not come with real authority when it does.
  • You are an analytics consultant who has built greenfield stacks for financial services clients and wants to own the outcome rather than hand it back at the end of the engagement.
  • You have killed a test stakeholders wanted to call a win — because the numbers didn't support it — and made that call land without losing the room.
  • The absence of infrastructure reads as opportunity, not obstacle.

Your first year

The first six months are infrastructure and attribution — event collection, warehousing, transformation, and visualisation layers selected and stood up; UUID tracking live across every marketing channel; data governance documented and adopted. Month six to nine is about the canonical data model: getting teams who currently run on different definitions of "Client" and "Trader" to agree on one, and building the pipeline that makes those definitions operational. By month twelve, every major product has real-time KPIs tied to business outcomes, the hypothesis-testing framework is running (not being debated), and marketing KPIs are in dashboards used weekly in actual decisions. Throughout: directing the work of embedded analysts across the org, raising the floor on what good looks like, and beginning to hire deliberately for the longer-term team.

The ask

What's the one architectural or attribution decision you've made from scratch that you're most proud of — and what would you do differently?

jobs.description:
Since our founding in 1996, Numerix has been at the vanguard of financial technology, providing quantitative analytics and software that redefine pricing and risk management across the financial markets. Through recent strategic acquisitions, Numerix has further strengthened its leadership position, empowering financial institutions worldwide to transform risk into opportunity with confidence. As AI reshapes capital markets technology, Numerix is focused on combining the speed and flexibility of AI with the deterministic, auditable, and governed calculations that financial institutions require.

The Product Architect, Oneview Engineering will work within the Product & Engineering organization to help develop the next generation of front-to-risk solution offerings for the financial markets industry.

Reporting directly to the Head of Engineering, Oneview, this is a senior individual contributor role that serves as a trusted partner to Engineering leadership, driving solution design quality, cross-functional alignment, and development readiness across the Oneview platform.

The Product Architect is responsible for bridging the gap between business intent and technical execution, translating complex product requirements into robust, scalable, end-to-end solution designs that Engineering teams can execute with clarity and confidence. Working at the intersection of Product Management, Business Analysis, Financial Engineering, Architecture, and Software Engineering, the Product Architect will partner closely with those teams to challenge assumptions, identify solution gaps, evaluate trade-offs, and ensure that complex features are fully understood before implementation begins.

The role requires a unique combination of financial domain expertise, practical technology fluency, and deep understanding of enterprise financial software platforms. It is ideal for someone who can operate comfortably across business, product, quantitative, and engineering discussions, turning ambiguity into clear solution direction and helping ensure consistent, high-quality execution across the platform.

What You'll Do:

  • Partner with Product Management, Business Analysts, Development Leads, and Software Architects to translate business and product requirements into clear, end-to-end solution designs.
  • Decompose complex features and workflows into implementable solutions, identifying business rules, dependencies, edge cases, cross-functional impacts, and delivery risks.
  • Drive development readiness by reviewing and refining requirements, user stories, process flows, acceptance criteria, and related artifacts before they enter Engineering execution.
  • Produce logical solution designs, workflow definitions, dependency maps, interface specifications, and other design artifacts that guide implementation using prototypes, examples, scripts, or mockups where.
  • Serve as a steward of Oneview's product architecture, ensuring solutions are placed in the appropriate layer, ownership and system boundaries remain clear, APls and integration interfaces are thoughtfully designed, and capabilities are reusable, scalable, and consistent across the platform.
  • Evaluate the impact of proposed solutions across data models, analytics, workflows, integrations, deployment architecture, upgrade paths, operational processes, and future platform evolution.
  • Identify and address non-functional requirements, including scalability, performance, maintainability, configurability, backward compatibility, Saas readiness, and operational supportability.
  • Work across Oneview modules and related Numerix products to ensure solutions are optimized from an end-to-end product perspective rather than a single-team or single-module perspective.
  • Facilitate design discussions and decision-making across Product, Financial Engineering, Architecture, and Engineering teams, reducing ambiguity and accelerating execution.
  • Influence and help shape Oneview's Al strategy by evaluating emerging Al capabilities, defining how Al should be incorporated into product workflows and platform services, and ensuring Al-driven solutions align with business needs, product architecture, and long-term platform direction.
  • Stay current with Oneview architecture, Numerix products, financial market workflows, and emerging technology trends relevant to the platform.

What We're Looking For:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field. Advanced degree, CFA, FRM, PRM, or equivalent professional experience is a plus.
  • 10+ years of experience in financial technology, capital markets software, quantitative analytics, product development, financial engineering, business analysis, solution architecture, or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of derivative trade lifecycle management from a front, middle, and/or back-office perspective.
  • Familiarity with pricing, valuation, risk, P&L, VaR, stress testing, market data, reference data, security master, trade capture, position management, and related capital markets workflows.
  • Knowledge of financial product structures, curve building, valuation models, pricing models, risk analytics, and exposure to multiple asset classes such as Fixed Income, Credit, Equities, Commodities, and FX.
  • Experience interpreting customer, product, or business needs and translating them into functional and technical requirements.
  • Practical technology fluency across APls, databases, data models, data integrations, cloud services, microservices, and software delivery processes.
  • Ability to work credibly with software engineers, development leads, product managers, business analysts, financial engineers, and client-facing teams.
  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to decompose high-level information, reconcile conflicting inputs, identify the underlying need, and convert ambiguity into clear solution direction.
  • Intermediate scripting or prototyping skills, preferably in Python, or equivalent ability to create lightweight examples that support solution.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to document assumptions, solution decisions, trade-offs, open questions, and risks.
  • Ability to work closely with others in a fast-paced, complex product development environment spread across multiple geographies.
  • Strong attention to detail, ownership mindset, and ability to manage multiple deliverables across stakeholders.

Where You’ll Work:

This is a hybrid role or remote role depending on the successful candidate's proximity to a Numerix office in the EMEA region.

An important note on salary:

The annual pay range for this position is based on the preferred primary location of the role which is listed above. If you are applying to this role at a location that is not the preferred primary location, please keep in mind the salary range will vary and may fall outside of what is listed. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

jobs.title: Senior Performance Creative Strategist
jobs.excerpt: Why This Role ExistsThis is a founding role — which means your ceiling is uncapped and your fingerprints will be on how an entire function works for years to come.
jobs.description:
Why This Role Exists
This is a founding role — which means your ceiling is uncapped and your fingerprints will be on how an entire function works for years to come.
You'll own how CDM identifies, develops, and scales creative — video and static — built Paid Social–first, with support for our Paid Search team, so our clients grow faster than their competitors can copy them.
Here's the bet we're making: creative is the most durable lever in performance marketing. Budgets, algorithms, audiences, and targeting all converge over time — everyone eventually gets access to the same tools. The creative is what still separates the winners from everyone else. CDM believes the agencies that dominate the next decade will be the ones that treat creative strategy as a rigorous, repeatable discipline instead of a guessing game.
You will be the person who builds that discipline here.

Key Responsibilities

Who We Are
Clever Digital Marketing is a performance marketing agency helping large home improvement companies across the US and Canada grow through Paid Social, Paid Search, CRO, and strategic advising.
We manage a large portfolio of accounts, an in-house creative team, and significant monthly ad spend. As we scale, we're building a stronger creative-strategy function to help clients find new creative winners — and to turn one-off learnings into repeatable systems that compound across every account.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

What You'll Own
This is a senior, strategic role. You won't be editing every asset or running campaigns day-to-day. Your job is to raise the quality of the thinking, research, and strategy behind everything we produce and test.
1. Generate net-new creative. Develop original concepts, messaging angles, hooks, formats, and storytelling approaches for video and static ads — not variations on the same three ideas.
2. Find the ideas before you have them. Run customer, competitor, and market research to uncover motivations, objections, and pain points that haven't been explored yet. Mine reviews, sales calls, and customer feedback for the insight that makes an ad work.
3. Turn performance into strategy. Analyze why creative wins or loses and translate it into clear next steps. Write sharp, actionable briefs grounded in customer insight, direct-response principles, and a defined testing hypothesis — and push iteration beyond surface-level hook and footage swaps.
4. Build the system. Create CDM's creative-strategy frameworks, brief standards, testing processes, and a shared learning repository. Spot what's working in one account and determine where it can be adapted across others.
5. Level up the whole team. Coach Media Buyers and editors so stronger creative thinking becomes a department-wide capability, not something that lives with one person. Partner with CRO to align messaging, personas, offers, and landing-page experiences. Provide direction for UGC, founder-led, and spokesperson-led formats.

6. Use AI as a force multiplier. Build AI-powered workflows and tools that accelerate research, ideation, and production for the entire team — more on that below.

What We're Looking For
  • 5+ years in performance-focused creative strategy.
  • Deep understanding of Meta advertising and direct-response creative.
  • Strong direct-response copywriting and short-form storytelling skills.
  • A track record of developing concepts from customer research and performance data — not just intuition.
  • Fluency with creative metrics (Hook Rate, Hold Rate, CTR, CPL) and the judgment to weigh them against lead quality and down-funnel performance.
  • Experience across multiple brands, accounts, or verticals.
  • A structured approach to testing — hypotheses, iteration strategy, isolating variables.
  • Demonstrated ability to build systems, processes, frameworks, or knowledge bases.
  • Advanced, practical experience using AI for research, analysis, ideation, workflow design, or creative enablement.
  • The ability to explain not just what you'd test, but how you found the opportunity and why you believe it will work.
  • Strong communication, prioritization, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • A bias for speed — you generate learning quickly without over-engineering every test.

What "AI-First" Means to Us

We are not looking for someone who asks AI to spit out scripts and hooks.
We're looking for someone who uses AI to:
  • Analyze customer reviews, calls, and feedback at scale.
  • Identify creative patterns across many accounts at once.
  • Build and maintain shared account context.
  • Surface cross-account testing opportunities.
  • Automate recurring creative research and reporting.
  • Improve the speed and quality of briefs and production workflows.
  • Build systems that help the whole team make better creative decisions.
You bring strong, independent creative judgment. AI is how you increase the depth, speed, and scale of that judgment. Familiarity with tools like Motion, Looker Studio, Asana, Slack, and Claude is a plus.

Nice to Have

  • Lead generation or high-ticket services experience.
  • Home improvement experience.
  • CRO and landing-page testing familiarity.
  • UGC, founder-led, or spokesperson-led creative experience.
  • Hands-on familiarity with editing or design tools.

What Success Looks Like

  • CDM consistently introduces genuinely new creative ideas instead of recycling the same concepts and formats.
  • Creative iterations are more deliberate, strategic, and evidence-based.
  • Media Buyers and editors produce stronger briefs and creative recommendations on their own.
  • Learnings are captured, shared, and applied across accounts.
  • AI-supported research and creative workflows are adopted department-wide.
  • CDM has a repeatable creative-strategy engine that gets stronger with every test.

Benefits

Benefits of Working at CDM
  • Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses
  • Flexible remote work environment with option for in-person collaboration (Vaughan, ON)
  • Group Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision, RRSP/401k Plan w/matching, more.
  • Company-provided MacBook computer
  • Home office budget and Clever merch delivery to get you started
  • Work Abroad Policy: Need a new working environment? Our work abroad policy supports this!
  • The chance to shape and grow a high-performing Client Success team
  • A culture of performance and respect where the best work happens with extreme ownership and accountability meets collaboration.
Clever Digital Marketing values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the team. We are happy to provide reasonable accommodations to candidates in need of support during the recruitment and selection process. Please note that artificial intelligence (AI) may be utilized during the interview or candidate evaluation process to support the fair and efficient screening, assessment, and selection of applicants.
