jobs.title: Manager II, Customer Success
jobs.excerpt: Who we areSamsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara’s Customer Success team ensures our customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. As Manager II on the US Scale Customer Success team, you will lead a team responsible for a high-volume portfolio of mid-market and large commercial customers in the private sector.

This is not a traditional CS leadership role. It is a builder role for a leader who drives renewal outcomes by making their team more effective — through better programs, cleaner signals, smarter automation, and sharper coaching. You will own the engagement model for your team: building the playbooks, building & improving digital, automated, lifecycle & AI-driven engagement programs, and coaching CSMs from activity-based to outcome-based work.

You will set the standard for what great Scale CS looks like, and personally step in when customers or situations demand it. The expectation is not just to run the team well — it is to make it fundamentally better.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will own:

  • Segmentation strategy: determine customer segmentation into service tiers and engagement models that blend targeted human interactions and scalable programs for a high-volume portfolio of mid-market accounts in the US private sector
  • Renewal outcomes: drive retention as the primary lens for every operating decision, not a reporting exercise
  • Expansion collaboration: partner with Sales to drive growth within accounts
  • Product adoption: work with CSMs to drive breadth and depth of product adoption
  • People leadership: hire, develop, and manage a team of CSMs, each managing portfolios of 100+ accounts
  • Productivity and efficiency: drive measurable output per CSM through AI, automation, digital programs, lifecycle workflows, and smart tooling integrations
  • AI-forward: champion experimentation and adoption of AI-powered workflows and tools to enhance customer engagement and team productivity
  • Risk management: identify and mitigate risk at scale using data-driven insights
  • Cross-functional leadership: partner with Sales, RevOps, Marketing, Product, and Business Technology to increase team productivity and improve customer experience
  • Escalation leadership: step into critical customer situations personally and providing leadership coverage when it matters, balancing strategic oversight with hands-on resolution

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years of experience in Customer Success or Account Management
  • 2+ years of direct people management experience leading CSMs or similar customer-facing roles with a portfolio of 100+ accounts each
  • Demonstrated experience building or significantly redesigning a scale, tech-touch, or digital CS model for pooled CSMs with measurable retention or expansion outcomes
  • Demonstrated ownership or significant influence over retention and expansion outcomes
  • Strong analytical capability; comfortable using data to drive prioritization, segmentation, and performance management.
  • Proven ability to lead through ambiguity, organizational change, and fast growth in a high-volume environment

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience at a SaaS company with a hardware or IoT component
  • Experience integrating AI into CS workflows to drive measurable team productivity
  • Advanced proficiency with Gainsight (or similar customer success platforms)
  • Experience partnering closely with Sales on expansion and account strategy

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary
$125,902—$190,440 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. jobs.title: CAD Plug In Developer
jobs.excerpt: Trilon is building a digital platform that gives engineers one place to manage, share and reuse their design data.
jobs.description:
Trilon is building a digital platform that gives engineers one place to manage, share and reuse their design data. The desktop tools our engineers use every day, Autodesk Civil 3D, the Bentley OpenX family (OpenRoads, OpenRail, OpenSite, OpenComms) and Esri ArcGIS Pro, need to connect to that platform directly.
As our Senior CAD Plugin Developer, you will own those connections. You will design and build the plugins that let an engineer export a design from their CAD tool into the platform, bring designs back by project, and keep spatial data in sync with ArcGIS. You will set the technical direction for our plugin work and be the team’s expert on CAD and GIS APIs and civil design data.
The hard part of this job is less the CAD APIs and more how designers actually work: when they save, what they reuse, where a plan set comes from, and what they will tolerate inside a design session. You will spend real time with civil designers so the plugins fit their workflow instead of interrupting it.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build the plugins. Design, build and ship production plugins for AutoCAD / Civil 3D (.NET, ObjectARX) and MicroStation / OpenX Designer SDKs (.NET and native SDKs).
  • Own the export path. Build the end-to-end flow from a click in the plugin to the platform: sign-in through the platform (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect from a desktop app, with tokens that persist between sessions), packaging the design, upload through platform APIs, and handling partial failures and retries.
  • Build the import path. Let users browse designs by project, pick files and download them into the CAD session through secure, time-limited download links.
  • Get the data right. Extract and convert civil objects (alignments, profiles, corridors, surfaces, pipe networks, feature lines) and their coordinate systems into open formats such as LandXML, IFC and GeoJSON, without losing data.
  • Connect to GIS. Build ArcGIS Pro add-ins and integrations that sync CAD spatial data with ArcGIS, including styles, spatial reference files and OGC-standard services.
  • Fit the designer’s workflow. Sit with civil designers, watch how they work in a session, and shape when and how the plugin asks for their attention. Validate output against real projects before it ships.
  • Instrument what you ship. Add usage and error events to the plugins so we can see how export and import perform in the field.
  • Package and support. Own installers, code signing, versioning across yearly Autodesk and Bentley releases, and deployment to engineers’ machines.
  • Partner with platform engineers. Work with the platform team on the REST and GraphQL APIs and the storage the plugins call, and on any third-party service integrations the plugins depend on.
  • Lead technically. Set plugin architecture and coding standards, review code, and mentor other developers on CAD and GIS APIs.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

  • 6+ years of professional software development, with at least 4 years building and shipping CAD plugins or extensions used in production.
  • Strong C# and .NET, and working C/C++ for native CAD APIs.
  • Deep experience with the AutoCAD and Civil 3D APIs; hands-on experience with the MicroStation SDK or one or more of the Bentley OpenX Designer SDKs (OpenRoads, OpenRail, OpenSite, OpenComms).
  • Working knowledge of civil design workflows and processes: how roadway, drainage, grading or site designers move from survey to model to plan set, what they reuse across projects, and where the time goes.
  • Experience calling REST and GraphQL APIs from desktop applications, including OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect sign-in and secure token storage.
  • Experience with coordinate systems, map projections and spatial data formats (LandXML, GeoJSON, shapefiles, geodatabases).
  • ArcGIS Pro SDK, ArcGIS REST APIs, Arcade, or QGIS development.
  • PostgreSQL / PostGIS or other spatial databases.

About Trilon

Trilon was formed with the vision of building the next Top 20 infrastructure consulting firm in North America by bringing together some of the nation’s best infrastructure consulting firms, focused on delivering practical and sustainable infrastructure solutions. Trilon is backed by Alpine Investors, a PeopleFirst Private Equity Firm. Trilon currently comprises 5,500+ staff across the US. For more information, visit www.trilon.com.

Pay Transparency
The base salary range for this role is indicated in the posting. This range reflects the company’s good faith estimate of the compensation for this position at the time of posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location.

The Senior Director serves as a primary point of coordination among partners and CSI’s Product, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Legal, Risk, Technology, and Operations teams. Responsibilities include evaluating partnership opportunities, supporting business cases and due diligence, negotiating and structuring agreements, coordinating partner onboarding and launches, overseeing renewals and partner exits, monitoring financial and operational performance, and resolving cross-functional issues that could affect partner or customer outcomes.


The Senior Director monitors partnership revenue, profitability, contractual obligations, customer feedback, market trends, and other key performance indicators to identify opportunities, address risks, and improve portfolio performance.


The Senior Director also leads the day-to-day work of the Strategic Partnerships team, assigns and prioritizes partner responsibilities, develops team members, and ensures appropriate coverage across CSI’s partner portfolio.   • Establish partner governance practices, performance standards, scorecards, and recurring business reviews.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Radar - Fraud and Abuse Prevention
jobs.excerpt: About the teamRadar helps businesses prevent fraud and abuse without getting in the way of legitimate customers.
jobs.description:
About the team

Radar helps businesses prevent fraud and abuse without getting in the way of legitimate customers. We combine machine learning powered by Stripe’s global network with intuitive dashboard experiences and developer APIs, to give our users comprehensive controls and insights to protect their business against threats ranging from payment fraud and card testing to bot and free trial abuse.

Fraud doesn’t stand still, and it isn’t limited to checkout. As businesses launch new products and business models, attackers find new ways to exploit them. We obsess about understanding those attacks, identifying defenses that work, and making sophisticated fraud prevention simple for the businesses that depend on us to help them protect and grow their revenue with confidence.

What you’ll do

As a product manager on the Radar team, you’ll work directly with customers to understand the novel fraud and abuse attacks they face, identify the most important problems to solve, and turn those insights into product strategy and a roadmap.

You’ll work at the intersection of customers, engineering, data science, design, and commercial teams to shape what we build and bring it to market. Your work will span the fraud and abuse detection and control capabilities at the heart of Radar and the user and developer experiences that put those capabilities into our customers’ hands.

This role requires both urgency and taste. You’ll move quickly as threats evolve, without compromising on reliability, craft, or the details that make complex products feel beautifully simple.

Responsibilities

  • Develop a deep understanding of the fraud and abuse landscape.
  • Investigate emerging attacks with customers, assess their financial and operational impact, and distinguish isolated incidents from opportunities to build broadly useful defenses.
  • Translate findings into a product strategy and roadmap, prioritizing the defenses that deliver the greatest customer and business impact.
  • Partner with engineering, data science, and design to explore signals, shape solutions, and rapidly turn effective defenses into scalable, reliable products.
  • Set the pace for the team by scoping the product thoughtfully, prioritizing ruthlessly, and executing with high rigor.
  • Work with sales, marketing, and customer-facing teams to validate demand, coordinate launches, and help customers adopt and maximize the value they get from new capabilities.
  • Own product performance, user experience, and business metrics to guide iteration and communicate progress.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years of Product Management experience
  • Highly analytical, with a rigorous approach to quantitative and qualitative evidence. You’re comfortable digging into data, writing SQL when needed, and defining metrics that connect product decisions to user outcomes.
  • Scrappy and resourceful, with experience taking products from zero to one. You find ways to test ideas quickly, learn from real users, and turn early solutions into products that scale.
  • Strong commercial and business acumen. You understand how customer problems translate into willingness to pay, adoption, and durable business value.
  • Proven cross-functional leadership, including experience partnering with B2B sales teams on customer discovery, product positioning, and adoption.
  • Experience shipping Dashboard and API products, with empathy for both end users and developers and an understanding of their different workflows.
  • Comfort with substantial ambiguity. You can set direction with incomplete information, make thoughtful trade-offs, and adapt as new evidence emerges.
  • Technical fluency to go deep with engineering and data teams on complex systems, understand constraints, and evaluate alternative approaches.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a talent for distilling complex customer problems into precise, actionable framing.
  • An ownership mindset and a high bar for product quality. You do what it takes to solve user problems and care deeply about the details of the experience.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building fraud prevention, risk, security, or ML powered products.
  • Experience developing machine learning powered products and evaluating trade-offs between detection effectiveness and customer friction.
  • Experience building tools for fraud analysts or risk teams, or developer products that support real-time decisions.
  • Software engineering, data science, or similar technical experience.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the Role:

Samsara is seeking a high-impact, strategic seller to lead the go-to-market execution for our newest frontier: AI Products. As an Enterprise Specialist (Overlay), you will partner with our Account Executives (AEs) to build deep partnerships with our largest, most complex accounts. You aren't just selling a tool; you are pioneering GTM, ensuring our customers realize continuous value from AI-driven automation.

About the Team:

This specialist team reports into a Sales Director (SD) and consists of specialist sellers aligned by segment and product. AEs on the team are charged with accelerating the growth of a new product and will be incentivized on quarterly product sales targets mapped to 1 or more regional directors for mainline sellers in the segment. Product Specialist sellers drive growth through strategic, high-value deal executing and enabling the segment overall to be successful.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the United States.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You have an innate curiosity about how businesses work: One day you’re meeting with a VP of Operations in waste management; the next, you’re diving into the logistics of a global food distributor. You seek to understand the "unit of value" for every customer.
  • You are an AI pragmatist: You understand that AI Products are about outcomes, not just "cool tech." You can translate LLM and agentic capabilities into tangible safety and efficiency gains for the physical world.
  • You build genuine, high-stakes relationships: Our customers operate in "boots-on-the-ground" industries. They value earned trust and partners who understand their operational realities.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.
  • You are a team Player: In an overlay role, your success is tied to the success of the broader account team. You lead through influence, not just authority.

In this role you will:

  • Architect deals that align Samsara’s AI Products value with customer use cases to provide maximum value and return on investment
  • Co-develop new product pipeline with ADRs/AEs across high potential “AI-ready” accounts
  • Drive high-touch pilot strategy and success metrics for early adoption
  • Partner with GTM and Product to feed back insights and help shape roadmap
  • Build frameworks, assets and insights that scale across the sales org

.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years in complex, full-cycle Enterprise sales.
  • 2+ years of direct experience selling in AI-based commercial models (e.g., Snowflake, AWS, Twilio, or AI-native platforms).
  • Proven Track Record: Consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts with $500k+ ARR transactions.
  • Deal Complexity: Demonstrated success navigating 6- and 7-figure deals involving multiple stakeholders (Legal, Procurement, InfoSec, and C-Suite).
  • Entrepreneurial Agility: Experience selling "Version 1.0" products where the playbook is still being written.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience working in a specialist/overlay co-selling with a mainline AE team.
  • 4+ years direct experience selling AI-based commercial models with a deep understanding of forecasting and expansion mechanics.
  • Strong grasp of AI/ML concepts and how AI Products differ from standard automation.

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) for full-time employees for this position is below. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary
$350,000—$350,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

jobs.description:
About HumanSignal

Real-world data is the competitive edge in AI.

HumanSignal is a human data partner for companies building AI models and products. Our customers ship better AI, faster, because we partner with their researchers from real-world data creation to annotation to delivery.

We design and create datasets from scratch, recruit and manage the domain experts who evaluate model output, and run everything through our own platform, Label Studio, the open-source standard for data labeling and evaluation, used by over 1 million practitioners worldwide.

We specialize in the operationally complex: real-world data collection, multimodal pipelines, and multi-step workflows. Advanced ML and AI teams use our enterprise platform to run their own data factories, and our services team to extend their reach where in-house capacity runs out.

If you want to do work that materially shapes how the next generation of AI products gets built, we'd love to talk.

Audio Editor – Multitrack Dialogue

  • Location: Remote
  • Type: Contract (20 to 35 hours per week, 2 to 4 weeks initially with potential to extend)
  • Duration: Immediate start; group training on Monday, October 27
You’ll master multitrack recordings from our production studio and deliver them to spec through our platform. Each session captures a user mic, an assistant mic and four channels from a Zoom field recorder. The four-channel portion is where most of the work lives: each channel needs individual leveling, noise reduction and timing alignment so the mix stays even across the stereo field. You’ll work from a rubric, hand off to QA, and flag recording issues (camera movement during dialogue, sync problems) back to the production team.
This is a hands-on editing role. We’re looking for people who can work channel by channel in a DAW, not people who rely on one-click AI cleanup tools.

What you’ll do

  • Master roughly one file per 3 hours: clean, denoise, level and align six tracks per session
  • Apply and adjust processing per channel; correct timing offsets between channels
  • Deliver files in the required format and loudness spec through our platform
  • Follow the QA rubric and incorporate feedback from reviewers
  • Note recurring audio problems so the studio team can fix them at the source

What we’re looking for

  • Proficiency in a professional DAW (Reaper, Pro Tools, Adobe Audition, Logic or similar)
  • Experience with multitrack dialogue editing and field recorder audio
  • Strong noise reduction skills (iZotope RX or comparable)
  • Ability to hear and correct timing and phase issues between channels
  • Consistency and speed; you can hit a quality bar repeatedly across dozens of files
  • Availability for full-time hours for at least the next two weeks

Nice to have

  • Background in podcast, film or broadcast post-production
  • Experience working to a rubric or client spec at volume
  • Familiarity with Zoom H-series or F-series recorders

Overview: Data Strategy and Governance

The Data Architect is responsible for designing and governing the end-to-end data landscape of our integrated supply chain e-commerce platform. You will create comprehensive data models, establish robust ETL pipelines to unify data from core systems (MES, WMS, OMS), and architect the infrastructure for real-time analytics, ensuring strict compliance with data privacy regulations like GDPR.

Internship Details

Duration: 3 months

Start Date: Immediate

Location: Remote

Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.

Key Responsibilities & Core Projects

You will transform raw system data into a structured asset, supporting both operational efficiency and business intelligence.

  • Data Modeling & Design: Design and maintain comprehensive conceptual, logical, and physical data models for all data domains: e-commerce transactions, customer behavior, internal tool usage, and supply chain records.

  • Data Integration (ETL): Architect and implement scalable ETL/ELT pipelines to efficiently aggregate, transform, and load data from disparate sources, including PostgreSQL 15 (MES, WMS, OMS modules) and internal applications.

  • Data Governance & Compliance: Define and enforce data governance policies, focusing heavily on GDPR compliance, data privacy, access control, and data quality standards.

  • Analytics Infrastructure: Design and implement the infrastructure for real-time analytics and business intelligence, ensuring data is readily available and optimized for consumption by reporting tools and the Analytics/BI module.

  • Retention & Archival: Define and plan data retention, archiving, and purging strategies, ensuring long-term data management efficiency and compliance.

  • Database Optimization: Collaborate with SRE and development teams to optimize database schemas and queries for both high transactional throughput and analytical reporting performance.

Required Technologies & Tools

Candidates must possess deep experience in data modeling, integration, and governance across diverse systems:

  • Database Mastery: Expert proficiency in PostgreSQL 15 (schema design, performance tuning, RLS principles) and caching technologies (Redis).

  • Data Warehousing/ETL: Proven experience designing and implementing scalable data pipelines and data warehouse structures.

Inbox and calendar management form part of the role, alongside broader responsibility for organising projects, improving workflows, preparing decisions and keeping commitments on track.

jobs.title: Interoperability & Standards Specialist (US)
jobs.excerpt: position details About the role Very few people get to see both how US interoperability regulation is written and how it plays out inside a working FHIR product.
jobs.description:
position details

About the role

Very few people get to see both how US interoperability regulation is written and how it plays out inside a working FHIR product. In this role, you’ll become one of them, and grow expertise that’s genuinely rare and valuable.

Firely builds FHIR-based interoperability software. Firely Server is ONC-certified health IT, and our digital quality measure pipeline is NCQA HEDIS certified. These certifications are commitments to our customers, and keeping them current is meaningful work with real deadlines. Much of our US business serves the payer market, where CMS rules such as the Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F) directly shape what our products must do.

That’s where you come in. You’ll own Firely’s US certifications end to end, keep us connected to the standards communities that shape our products, and act as our early-warning system for everything CMS, ASTP/ONC and NCQA publish. It’s a hands-on role: you’ll personally prepare and submit the quarterly certification packages, run measure test decks through our pipeline, and write the summaries the product team relies on.

You’ll be part of the Product team and work closely with Alexander Zautke, our VP of Product & Standards. Alexander sets the direction on regulatory and standards strategy and decides what lands on the roadmap. You’ll drive the execution, dig into the details, and bring back the analysis our decisions are built on. We’re looking for someone self-sufficient who brings ideas and solutions forward on their own. Over time, you’ll take on more of the analysis and the calls yourself.

This is an engineering-minded role, not a pure compliance one, so you don’t need to be a regulatory expert. What matters most is strong hands-on experience with interoperability and the US healthcare system, and real curiosity about the regulatory landscape around it.

Your core responsibility: certification

  • ONC/ASTP certification maintenance. Prepare and submit the quarterly (g)(10) maintenance package to Drummond, our ONC-ACB: summary of changes, Inferno test results and the required attestation forms. File SVAP submissions when we adopt a new standards version, and complete the bi-annual attestations in CHPL.
  • Real World Testing. Write the annual RWT plan and results report, and run the testing behind them. RWT is currently under a moratorium; you'll pick it up when it restarts.
  • NCQA HEDIS measure certification. For each measure, pull the test decks, run them through Firely Server and our dQM pipeline, review the output, submit to NCQA and work the tickets until the measure passes. As Firely's day-to-day contact with NCQA, you keep the correspondence off our engineers' plates so they can focus on fixing what you find.
  • Certified version transitions. When a major Firely Server version ships, analyze the release notes against the (g)(10) criteria, work with Drummond to move the certification, and file the withdrawal request for the retired version.
  • Organizational obligations. Track the non-product (g)(10) requirements (Information Blocking, Assurances, Communications), keep our public certification disclosures accurate, and flag gaps early. Accountability sits with the VP of Product & Standards; you make sure nothing is missed.

Regulatory monitoring

You make sure nothing relevant gets past us, and that what does arrives in a form the product team can act on. You and the VP of Product & Standards agree which areas to watch closely.
  • Weekly scan. Work through the Federal Register, CMS, ASTP/ONC and NCQA for proposed and final rules, RFIs and RFCs. Screen them against the topics that matter to us: FHIR, digital quality measures, USCDI, prior authorization, payer APIs.
  • Written analysis. For every relevant rule, write a summary: what it requires, what it means for our products and customers, and what you recommend. Write it even when the answer is "no action needed"; that conclusion is worth recording. Where a rule needs more, you work with the VP of Product & Standards on a deeper analysis.
  • Analysis into work. Translate product impact into Confluence pages and Jira tickets that engineering can pick up.
  • Regulatory tracker. Keep it current so anyone at Firely can see what is coming and when.
  • Comment letters. Track deadlines, gather input from across Firely, draft our responses to CMS and ONC, get sign-off and submit on regulations.gov.
  • Stay current. Attend ONC roundtables, CMS seminars and similar sessions.

Standards community work

Firely helps build the standards we implement. We are active in DQIC (the technical workgroup, plus its CQL unit testing and tooling subgroups), the HL7 Da Vinci Project, the HL7 FHIR Quality Accelerator, the HL7 CQI Workgroup, HL7 Connectathons on the DQM track, and ONC community forums. You manage Firely's communication and work items across these groups, and report back on any action we need to take to stay compliant and competitive.
  • Prepare. Pull together background on agenda items and ballot topics, summarize where things stand, and get our position ready so the VP of Product & Standards walks in briefed.
  • Follow up. Track what was decided, turn outcomes into Confluence pages and Jira tickets, and chase the items that belong to us.
  • Connectathon groundwork. Set up the test environment, prepare our FHIR server and DQM test tooling, work through PR testing, pass validation issues to engineering and write up the results.
  • Administration. Register Firely's US members for Connectathons and Working Group Meetings, track ballot and comment deadlines, and keep our participation in good order.

You'll join meetings yourself where it helps, some regularly and some occasionally; which one is a conversation with the VP of Product & Standards. As you build standing in these communities, you take on more of the representation directly. That is a growth path, not a starting requirement.

Also part of the role: prototyping and technical writing

Alongside the core work, you'll contribute in two further areas.
  • Prototypes. Help the VP of Product & Standards build prototypes that test ideas for Firely Server's product strategy. Your fluency with interoperability standards, combined with AI tools, helps us explore those ideas quickly.
  • Technical writing. Contribute internal memos on our certifications and help keep technical documentation up to date.

Who you are

We expect roughly 3–5 years of relevant experience, but we care more about the combination of interoperability and US healthcare experience than the years.
  • You're comfortable with the technology. You can run software yourself, read logs and test output, and work out why something failed before asking someone else. You don't need to write production code, but you can read a FHIR resource, follow a validation error, and work with APIs and test tooling without hand-holding. Experience with CQL is a real advantage.
  • You can read regulation and say what it means, or you're keen to learn. You can work through a 300-page proposed rule and come back with two paragraphs on what actually matters to us. You're comfortable saying "this one doesn't affect us" when that's the answer.
  • You connect the two. The value of this role is the link between a regulatory requirement and what our product does. You enjoy sitting in that gap.
  • You write clearly. Memos, analyses, documentation and comment letters are a core part of the job.
  • You own your deadlines. Certification runs on fixed dates that don't move, and you keep track of them without being reminded.
  • You're self-sufficient and work well with senior stakeholders. You take direction and context from the VP of Product & Standards and come back with work that's done, not work that needs redoing. You ask when you're stuck and push back when something doesn't add up.
  • You're curious about AI. Firely embraces AI. We want you to explore and get creative with how it can make our work faster without making it worse, and how it can shape our products and what we offer clients.
  • You're based in the US and understand the US healthcare market, ideally including payers.

Bonus points

None of these are required, but any one of them will make your application stand out.
  • Hands-on experience with ONC/ASTP certification: Inferno, CHPL, SVAP, Real World Testing, or working with an ACB such as Drummond
  • Experience with NCQA HEDIS measure certification or digital quality measures
  • Working knowledge of CQL
  • Experience with CMS payer interoperability requirements, such as CMS-0057-F
  • Experience at a certified health IT vendor, an EHR company or a health plan
  • Existing participation in HL7, Da Vinci, DQIC or similar
  • Experience drafting or coordinating formal regulatory comment letters

If you're technical and want to move into regulatory work, this role is built for you. If you know the regulatory side well but have less hands-on FHIR experience, tell us too.

How you'll grow

There is real room to grow here. We would rather grow you into more than hire over you.

You start by executing the certification work and doing the first pass on regulatory analysis, with the VP of Product & Standards setting priorities and reviewing your conclusions. As your judgement builds, you take more of the calls yourself: which rules matter, what we should recommend, and where we should push back. Over time you take on the outward-facing work too, presenting in workgroups, contributing to our comment letters and briefing customers on what's coming.

Benefits we offer

  • Fully remote working environment
  • 401(k), health and medical benefits, life and disability insurance
  • 22 vacation days
  • Annual learning & development budget
  • Home office budget

Practicalities

  • Location: Remote within the US.
  • Working with a Dutch team: Firely is headquartered in Amsterdam, and our product and engineering teams are largely in Europe, so expect some early-morning overlap. In exchange, your afternoons are quieter and allow for focus time or US team collaboration.
  • Travel: Around 4–5 week-long trips a year for Connectathons, HL7 Working Group Meetings and industry events. Plus,annual trips to Amsterdam for team building during our International Week!
  • Your Team Lead: You report to Alexander Zautke, VP of Product & Standards, and sit in the Product team.
  • Salary: $90,000-$110,000 annual base salary.

jobs.title: Head of People & Organizational Development
jobs.excerpt: Location: Remote, within 6 hours of US Eastern Time About SPUNSPUN (Society for the Protection of Underground Networks) is a startup NGO with a mission to map and protect the mycorrhizal fungal networks that regulate Earth’s climate and ecosystems.
jobs.description:
Location: Remote, within 6 hours of US Eastern Time

About SPUN

SPUN (Society for the Protection of Underground Networks) is a startup NGO with a mission to map and protect the mycorrhizal fungal networks that regulate Earth’s climate and ecosystems. These fungi draw down approximately 13 billion tons of CO2 each year, yet they have been largely overlooked by science, policy, and practice.

Since our founding in 2021, we’ve built a global data platform to make these invisible networks measurable. Through our Underground Explorers program and network of over 700 Science Associates across more than 80 countries, with the majority in the Global South, we generate high-resolution biodiversity maps and ML-powered tools that integrate mycorrhizal data into climate, conservation, restoration, and land management decisions.

Our work spans laboratory research, data science, and robotics through to locally led field applications, and we’ve begun working with policymakers and restoration practitioners to apply our findings on the ground. With strong backing from leading foundations and growing momentum in international policy circles, we’re now at an inflection point: scaling these efforts across more landscapes, institutions, and countries over the long term.

That next phase calls for new capabilities. We’re strengthening our data science and impact strategy capabilities alongside our research, and have recently brought in leaders in global policy and impact, partnerships and adoption, and restoration science. Over the next two to three years, we expect to add people at every level, from directors to managers and coordinators. Doing this efficiently, across new disciplines and with a team spread across many countries, is a real organizational challenge.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Head of People & Organizational Development to shape how SPUN works as it grows. This is not a traditional HR role. Day-to-day HR administration will sit with a dedicated Operations Manager. Your focus is the organization itself: how our people collaborate, make decisions, develop, and use the tools available to them to do their best work.

You will work closely with senior leadership across three connected areas:

Ways of working. Design the structures, rhythms, and practices that keep a distributed, multidisciplinary team aligned and moving quickly. That covers how decisions get made and how knowledge gets shared. It also covers how scientists, data scientists, policy specialists, and partnership leads work together toward shared goals.

Tools and technology. Shape the tools we rely on so they actually serve the work. This includes AI, which we believe can help expand what a small, distributed organization can accomplish in research, operations, and partnerships, but caution is also needed. The goal is not simply rolling out new tools—it is building the skills, judgment, and confidence to use them well without compromising scientific integrity.

Culture and leadership. Help our culture scale as new teams and leaders join. That means developing managers, building feedback and growth practices, and making sure people from very different disciplines and places feel part of one organization.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Design & Growth

  • Design and evolve SPUN’s organizational structure as we grow, so that teams, roles, reporting lines, and leadership responsibilities support our strategy.
  • Partner with senior leadership to anticipate the capabilities SPUN will need as we expand into new disciplines, and shape a thoughtful approach to hiring across levels.
  • Assess organizational health regularly, using clear indicators to identify where structure, capacity, or ways of working are creating friction or limiting impact.
  • Work with the Operations Manager to ensure people policies and processes reflect SPUN’s values and work well across the countries where we operate.

Ways of Working

  • Design the operating rhythms, decision-making processes, and planning practices that keep a distributed team aligned and moving quickly.
  • Strengthen how knowledge is captured and shared across the organization, so that work doesn’t depend on a single person, meeting, or time zone.
  • Improve how scientists, data scientists, policy specialists, and partnership leads collaborate toward shared goals, including the handoffs between research and applied work.

Tools & AI Adoption

  • Shape SPUN’s core tools and how we use them, making sure they benefit the research, our people, the organization, and our interactions with partners and the public.
  • Partner with senior leadership to develop SPUN’s approach to AI. Identify where it can meaningfully increase our impact and capacity, while weighing the implications for our mission and people.
  • Work with team leads to identify high-value AI use cases and the workflows, roles, and skills needed to make the most of them.
  • Build AI fluency across the organization through training, peer learning, experimentation, and practical resources tailored to different roles and levels of technical expertise.
  • Create ways for teams to share experiments, emerging practices, and lessons learned, so that adoption becomes a collective capability rather than a collection of individual efforts.

Culture & Connection

  • Create the conditions for a healthy, ambitious, and inclusive culture across a globally distributed organization, including practical approaches to team health, feedback, conflict resolution, and trust-building.
  • Build intentional opportunities for connection across time zones, disciplines, and teams, recognizing that many colleagues rarely work together in person.
  • Design and facilitate retreats, team sessions, and leadership gatherings that strengthen relationships and improve how we work together.
  • Design onboarding that brings new team members into SPUN’s culture and ways of working, not just its systems.
  • Develop a thoughtful approach to recognizing team and individual achievements.

Leadership, Performance & Development

  • Partner with senior leaders and managers to strengthen their ability to lead people as SPUN grows, with clear expectations for management and leadership.
  • Establish effective practices for feedback, goal-setting, development conversations, and performance reviews, so people understand what success looks like in their roles and how they can grow.
  • Develop progression pathways, including support for people moving from individual contributor roles into management.
  • Identify opportunities for learning and professional development across the organization.

Required Qualifications

Organizational builder. You have 7+ years of experience helping organizations scale and build culture, trust, connection, and accountability, ideally where people work remotely across time zones.

Strategist who builds. You can shape the strategy and then roll up your sleeves to build the processes, frameworks, and systems yourself.

Deeply curious about people. You want to understand what motivates people, how teams function, and what gets in the way of people doing their best work. You listen carefully and get to the real problem quickly.

Trusted leadership partner. You are comfortable advising senior leaders and challenging their thinking when necessary, while building strong relationships and credibility. You handle sensitive information and complex interpersonal situations with maturity and care.

Experienced in changing how people work. You have led the adoption of new tools, technologies, or ways of working, including AI. You know that lasting change depends on training, change management, and building confidence, not just rollout.

Excellent communicator. You communicate equally well with scientists, data scientists, policy and partnership specialists, and senior leadership, adapting your approach to different audiences.

Mission-driven. You are excited by SPUN’s mission and motivated to build the organizational conditions that allow a pioneering environmental NGO to have greater impact.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a science, research, environmental, or impact-driven organization.
  • Experience in a globally distributed organization operating across multiple countries and employment jurisdictions.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary teams that span science, policy, partnerships, and operations.
  • Experience building career frameworks, performance systems, or development programs from scratch.
  • Hands-on experience with AI tools and a genuine interest in how they will change the way organizations work.

Job Description

Candidates located in the Southwest or Northwest (WA, OR, CA or AZ) regions are strongly preferred.


The role is accountable for performance and compliance for assigned protocols and sites in a country.

Under the oversight of the CRA-Manager the person ensures compliance of study conduct with ICH/GCP and country regulations, our company's policies and procedures, quality standards and adverse event reporting requirements internally and externally.

Acts as primary site contact and site manager throughout all phases of a clinical research study, taking overall responsibility of allocated sites.

Actively develops and expands the territory for clinical research, finding and developing new sites.

Participates in internal meetings and workstreams as SME for monitoring processes and

Systems.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Develops strong site relationships and ensures continuity of site relationships through all phases of the trial.

  • Good understanding and working knowledge of clinical research, phases of clinical trials, current GCP/ICH & country clinical research law & guidelines.
  • Good understanding of Global, Country/Regional Clinical Research Guidelines and ability to work within these guidelines.
  • Hands on knowledge of Good Documentation Practices.
  • Proven Skills in Site Management including management of site performance and patient recruitment.

  • Good IT skills (Use of MS office, use of various clinical IT applications on computer, tablet and mobile devices) and ability to adapt to new IT applications on various devices.
  • Ability to understand and analyze data/metrics and act appropriately.
  • Capable of managing complex issues, works in a solution-oriented manner.
  • Performs root cause analysis and implements preventative and corrective action.

Behavioral Competency Expectations:

  • Effective time management, organizational and interpersonal skills, conflict management, problem solving skills.
  • Demonstrated high level of monitoring skill with independent professional judgement.
  • Able to work highly independently across multiple protocols, sites and therapy areas.
  • High sense of accountability / urgency. Ability to set priorities and handle multiple tasks simultaneously in a changing environment.
  • Works effectively in a matrix multicultural environment. Ability to establish and maintain culturally sensitive working relationships.
  • Demonstrates commitment to Customer focus.
  • Works with high quality and compliance mind-set.
  • Positive mindset, growth mindset, capable of working independently and being self-driven.
  • Demonstrates and projects professional demeanor and communication consistent with organizational policies and practices.

Experience and Educational Requirements:

About Us

WeVote is a nonpartisan get-out-the-vote nonprofit startup and a celebrated Fast Forward nonprofit technology grantee. WeVote is a movement of over 120 passionate volunteers (starting with the founders) who are building open-source mobile technologies that touch and mobilize millions of voters on Election Day. We observe that many voters are busy, distracted, and impatient. We have a goal of providing a complete voting experience in 8 minutes, including the download of our app ("WeVote Ballot Guide, @WeVote"). More information is at See Twitter @WeVote. You will have the opportunity to touch the lives of millions of Americans and be part of a movement and product that will receive national attention. You’ll gain an opportunity to grow within the WeVote movement and meet other volunteers who are like-minded and interested in building a valuable application to empower voters across the United States. As an HR Operations Manager, you will own the day-to-day relationships for a portfolio of high-growth startups, serving as each client’s primary point of contact and trusted HR partner. You will stay closely connected to client needs, anticipate priorities, and ensure they receive responsive, high-quality support.

Reporting to the HR Director, you will lead a team of HR Generalists and Philippines-based HR Specialists responsible for onboarding, employee changes, benefits administration, payroll support, recordkeeping, and other core HR operations. You will set priorities, delegate work, remove roadblocks, and provide the oversight needed to ensure the team’s work is accurate, timely, and consistent.

You'll be the voice on the client calls. When a founder wants to terminate someone in California next week, when a client hires their first employee in New York, when a harassment complaint lands with no precedent behind it — that's your call to lead to lead your team to the right decision.

If you have built or managed an HR function in a fast-growing organization, this role offers the opportunity to apply that experience across a portfolio of companies, with a team to lead and support.

What makes this role different

  • Direct management responsibility. You’ll lead and develop a distributed HR team, set priorities, delegate work, provide feedback, and address performance concerns when needed.
  • Ownership of client relationships. You’ll serve as the primary HR contact for founders and client leadership, providing practical guidance and taking responsibility for the quality and timeliness of the team’s work.
  • Broad compliance exposure. You’ll support clients across multiple states, including California, New York, Washington, and Colorado, as well as international contractors and EOR arrangements.
  • Clear boundaries around legal matters. You’ll be expected to recognize when an issue falls outside the scope of HR guidance and advise the client to consult qualified employment counsel.
  • A collaborative way of working. Client communications, documents, and processes are shared across the team to support visibility, review, feedback, and continuous learning.

What you'll own

The team

  • Lead a team of HR Generalists who oversee the day-to-day work of our Philippines-based HR Specialists.
  • Assign client coverage, set priorities across the portfolio, and manage capacity.
  • Review important work before it goes to a client, including agreements, filings, handbooks, and payroll output.
  • Coach and develop the people under you, including performance conversations and hiring input.
  • Build and improve the processes, templates, and playbooks the team uses.

The client relationship

  • Serve as the main point of contact for founders and client leadership.
  • Lead recurring client calls and stay informed about each client’s priorities and upcoming needs.
  • Handle the escalations your team can't resolve, and know which ones should never reach them in the first place.
  • Translate risk into decisions a founder can actually make.

Compliance and risk(you own the outcome; your team does much of the execution)

  • Federal, state, and applicable international employment compliance across the client portfolio.
  • Keep the team on top of contract renewals, policy deadlines, filing dates, and other compliance deadlines.
  • Government reporting and registrations, including EEO-1, ACA, and state registrations.
  • Set the standards for employment agreements, offer letters, separation agreements, and policy documents; provide final approval and personally draft more complex documents when needed.
  • Oversee the implementation and ongoing maintenance of employee handbooks, state addenda, and required compliance notices.
  • Workers’ compensation, EPLI, and other employment-related insurance programs.

Employee relations(this one stays with you)

  • Conduct workplace investigations and prepare documentation that holds up under scrutiny
  • Guide clients through performance management, accommodations, leave, and terminations
  • Support client managers through difficult conversations without taking the conversation from them

What you'll bring

Required

  • 6+ years in HR operations, compliance, or a senior generalist role, including at least 2 years directly managing or reviewing the work of other HR professionals
  • Client-facing or multi-entity experience — consulting, outsourced HR, PEO, or a multi-entity corporate role. You'll be advising people who don't report to you and can overrule you.
  • Demonstrated multi-state compliance ownership, including California
  • Experience conducting workplace investigations and documenting them
  • Hands-on background across the full stack your team runs — payroll, onboarding, benefits, PEO, HRIS. You won't do most of it day to day, but you'll review all of it, and you can't review what you've never done.
  • The ability to run a client call alone and hold the room when the answer isn't good news
  • SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR
  • Uses good judgment to make informed decisions and recognize when an issue should be escalated.
  • Possesses strong professional judgment, makes informed decisions, and recognizes when matters should be escalated or delegated.

Strongly preferred

  • Experience managing offshore or distributed teams
  • PHR-CA or California-specific compliance depth
  • Startup or VC-backed client experience
  • International employment, EOR, or global contractor exposure
  • Leave administration depth — FMLA, state leave programs, ADA interactive process
  • Bachelor's degree in HR, business, or a related field

Compensation and benefits

$115,000 – $125,000, depending on experience, location, and qualifications.

  • Health, dental, vision with employer contributions
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Paid Time Off
  • Fully remote role
  • SHRM or HRCI recertification support and professional development budget

Application review → 15 minute call with recruiter → practical exercise → 30-minute intro call → technical conversation with HR Ops Manager → final conversations with HR Director & CEO → paid trial onboarding. We aim to move from first call to decision in 3-4 weeks.

jobs.excerpt: Most accounting managers spend years going deep on one company's books.
jobs.description:
Most accounting managers spend years going deep on one company's books. This role goes wider.

You'll own the close for a portfolio of funded, high-growth startups — a Shopify brand with real inventory and landed costs one day, and a SaaS company with deferred revenue and equity ownership the next. You'll be on the client calls. You'll manage a team of offshore accountants who handle the transactional work so you can focus on review, judgment, and the conversations with the controller and founders.

If you've been the person who could be advising clients but keeps getting pulled into reconciliations, this is the step up.

What makes this seat different

  • Portfolio variety Tech, consumer products, retail, manufacturing, and services clients. Inventory and cost accounting, revenue recognition, lease accounting, and equity accounting — often in the same month.
  • You manage a team You'll directly lead our offshore accounting team: assigning work, reviewing output, and raising their ceiling. Real management experience, not a dotted line.
  • A modern stack, not a legacy ERP Puzzle, Ramp, Rho, Rippling, Carta, and Numeral are good examples. You'll leave here fluent in the tooling startups actually run on.
  • A path to Controller You'll work side by side with our Controllers on every engagement. We promote from within, so when you’re ready you’d get considered for a controller position.
  • Genuine transparency Drafts, working files, and client communications are visible across the team. Nobody works in a silo, and nobody gets blindsided in a client meeting. It means your work gets reviewed — and it means you learn from everyone else's.

What you'll own

The monthly close, for multiple clients
  • Generate timely, accurate monthly financial statements
  • Review and guide the offshore team's work product
  • Reconciliations, accruals, and deferred journal entries
  • Update financial models and cash forecasts with actuals
  • Manage client budgets
The client relationship
  • Engage in recurring client calls and respond to founder requests directly
  • Translate the numbers into something a non-finance founder can act on
  • Partner with our Controllers on strategic and advisory work
Accounting operations(you own the outcome; your team does much of the execution)
  • AR — invoicing and collections
  • AP — bill processing and vendor setup
  • Payroll and benefit clearing account reconciliations, including 401(k) and medical
  • Insurance audits and renewals
  • Inventory and landed costs
  • Sales tax management and compliance
Tax and compliance coordination
  • Work with external partners on federal and state income tax returns (C Corp, S Corp, LLC)
  • Annual state filings and franchise taxes
  • Local business registrations, sales and use tax, R&D tax credits, W-9s and 1099s

What you'll bring

Required
  • 7+ years of accounting experience, including at least 2 years managing or reviewing the work of other accountants
  • Experience serving multiple clients or entities at once; public accounting, outsourced accounting, or a multi-entity corporate role
  • Strong working knowledge of US GAAP; financial statement presentation, revenue recognition, deferred revenue, prepaid and accrued expenses, fixed assets
  • Hands-on ownership of a full-cycle monthly close
  • Fluency in QuickBooks Online or Xero
  • Strong Google Sheets skills — pivot tables, SUMIFS, model maintenance
  • Bachelor's degree, accounting or finance concentration preferred
  • Comfortable leading a client call without a Controller in the room
Strongly preferred
  • CPA, or CPA-eligible and pursuing it
  • Big 4 or national public accounting background
  • Startup or VC-backed client experience
  • Inventory, manufacturing, or cost accounting exposure
  • Equity accounting exposure
You'll pick up here if you don't have it Puzzle · Expensify · Ramp · Rho · Brex · Bill.com · Settle · Mercury Bill Pay · Gusto · JustWorks · Rippling · Warp · Sequoia · Deel · RemoFirst · Shopify · Amazon FBA · Walmart Seller Central · Avalara · Numeral · TaxJar · Pulley · Carta · AngelList · Stripe · PayPal · Cin7 · Fishbowl · SOS

Compensation and benefits

$100,000 - $120,000, depending on experience and location.

We have an amazing benefits package which includes:
  • Health, dental, and vision
  • 401(k) and matching
  • PTO policy
  • 100% fully remote

Application review → 15 minute call with recruiter → practical exercise → 30-minute intro call → technical conversation with a Controller → final conversations with HR Director & CEO → paid trial onboarding. We aim to move from first call to decision in 3-4 weeks.

Head of Portfolio Growth

Location: Canada, Remote

About Niricson

At Niricson, we believe the world's most critical infrastructure deserves better intelligence.

From hydroelectric dams and bridges to airfields, utilities, transportation networks, and industrial assets, aging infrastructure is a growing global challenge. Traditional inspection methods are often slow, subjective, risky, and difficult to scale.

By combining robotics, AI, advanced sensing technologies, geospatial analytics, and data intelligence, Niricson helps infrastructure owners make smarter, safer, and more proactive decisions about the assets their communities depend on every day.

About the role

Niricson is looking for a Head of Portfolio Growth to lead the expansion of our existing customer base across infrastructure owners, public-sector agencies, utilities, airports, transportation authorities, and large asset-intensive organizations.

This is a senior commercial leadership role focused on turning initial customer engagements into broader, multi-asset, recurring, portfolio-wide relationships. You will build the strategy, operating rhythm, account planning discipline, and customer expansion motion required to grow Niricson's footprint within existing enterprise and public-sector customers.

This role is ideal for a commercial leader who has sold complex technology, data, inspection, asset management, or infrastructure solutions into government, utilities, transportation, engineering, or other asset-intensive markets.

What You’ll Do

  • Own Portfolio Expansion

Lead Niricson's growth strategy for existing customers, with a focus on expanding from initial projects into larger, multi-site, multi-asset, and recurring customer relationships.

  • Build Strategic Account Plans

Create account plans for key customers, including stakeholder maps, expansion paths, renewal risks, procurement timelines, budget cycles, executive relationships, and multi-year growth opportunities.

  • Drive Expansion Revenue

Own expansion bookings, upsell, cross-sell, renewals, and account penetration across Niricson's existing customer portfolio.

  • Partner with Customer Success and Delivery

Work closely with Customer Success, Delivery, Product, Engineering, and Data teams to ensure customer outcomes translate into long-term commercial growth.

  • Engage Executive Buyers

Build relationships with senior stakeholders across asset management, engineering, operations, capital planning, finance, risk, innovation, and executive leadership.

  • Turn Projects into Programs

Develop repeatable motions to move customers from one-time inspections or pilot deployments into broader portfolio-level adoption of Niricson's platform and analytics.

  • Shape Commercial Packaging

Partner with leadership to refine pricing, packaging, renewal structures, expansion strategy, and recurring revenue models based on customer needs and market feedback.

  • Build the Portfolio Growth Function

Create the playbook, processes, KPIs, CRM discipline, team structure, and reporting cadence required to establish a scalable Portfolio Growth organization.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of experience in enterprise sales, strategic account management, customer expansion, or commercial leadership.
  • Proven success expanding existing enterprise or public-sector accounts.
  • Experience selling into one or more of the following markets: infrastructure, utilities, transportation, public sector, municipalities, airports, dams, engineering, asset management, inspection, NDT, geospatial, digital twin, robotics, or industrial analytics.
  • Strong understanding of complex B2B or public-sector sales cycles, procurement processes, renewals, and budget timing.
  • Ability to translate technical capabilities into executive-level business value.
  • Experience building account plans and managing multi-stakeholder customer relationships.
  • Comfort working in a growth-stage company where systems, processes, and teams are still being built.
  • Strong commercial judgment, executive presence, and ability to operate both strategically and hands-on.
  • Experience working with CRM systems and revenue reporting discipline.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with infrastructure asset owners such as utilities, DOTs, airports, municipalities, transit agencies, hydro operators, or government infrastructure departments.
  • Background in SaaS, data analytics, AI, robotics, inspection technology, asset management software, or digital twin platforms.
  • Experience converting services-led revenue into recurring platform or subscription revenue.
  • Existing network across Canadian or U.S. public infrastructure markets.
  • Experience managing account managers, customer success managers, or strategic account teams.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 6–12 months, you will have:

  • Built a clear account segmentation and portfolio growth strategy.
  • Created strategic account plans for Niricson's highest-priority customers.
  • Established a repeatable expansion and renewal operating cadence.
  • Improved visibility into expansion pipeline and customer health.
  • Helped convert existing customers into larger, multi-asset programs.
  • Created stronger alignment between Sales, Customer Success, Delivery, Product, and Executive leadership.

Key Success Metrics

  • Expansion bookings
  • Net revenue retention
  • Gross revenue retention
  • Renewal rate
  • Multi-asset / multi-site customer growth
  • Expansion pipeline created
  • Strategic account penetration
  • Executive stakeholder coverage
  • Customer health and expansion readiness

Why Join Niricson

This is a chance to help define a new category of infrastructure intelligence.

You will work with a team applying robotics, AI, sensing, and analytics to some of the world's most important physical assets. You will help infrastructure owners move from reactive inspection to proactive, data-driven asset management.

As Niricson grows, this role will have the opportunity to shape a core commercial function, influence company strategy, and build long-term customer relationships across some of the most important infrastructure markets in North America and globally.

Who we are…

Verra Mobility is a global leader in smart mobility. We develop technology-enabled solutions that help the world move safely and easily. We are fostering the development of safe cities, working with police departments and municipalities to install over 4,000 red-light, speed, and school bus stop arm safety cameras across North America. We are also creating smart roadways, serving the world's largest commercial fleets and rental car companies to manage tolling transactions and violations for over 8.5 million vehicles. And we are a leading provider of connected systems, processing nearly 165 million transactions each year across 50+ individual tolling authorities.

Position Overview

The Implementation Consultant combines business requirements management and technical documentation expertise to support the implementation of complex, high-priority technology programs for state and local government clients. Working in partnership with the Project Leader (Project Manager or Program Manager), this role is responsible for gathering, validating, managing, and documenting client business rules, operational workflows, and technical and business requirements that directly impact program compliance, system configuration, and execution.

The Client Implementation Consultant collaborates closely with cross-functional teams, including Engineering, Legal, Sales, Product, and Operations, to translate client needs and applicable regulatory requirements into accurate, actionable implementation deliverables. This role requires exceptional attention to detail, sound judgment, strong organizational skills, and the ability to manage complex documentation and competing priorities while ensuring alignment with client expectations, business objectives, software capabilities, and applicable state and local legislative requirements.

Essential Responsibilities

· Business Requirements Management: Lead and coordinate the BRQ process by managing internal and external stakeholder contributions, validating submitted information, and ensuring requirements are accurately captured and documented within established timelines for client-specific system configuration business and technical requirements.

· Client Needs Assessment: Develop a thorough understanding of client business objectives, operational workflows, business rules, and implementation requirements to ensure solutions align with client needs and program expectations.

· Implementation Coordination and Reporting: Work in conjunction to support the Project Leader for implementation milestones and deliverables. Proactively identify, document, and communicate implementation risks, dependencies, and challenges, coordinating timely resolution with the appropriate stakeholders.

· Program Document Development: Collaborate with Engineering, Software Development, Legal, and other stakeholders to draft, review, finalize, and deliver program-specific documentation, including citations, notices, certifications, affidavits, and other required materials.
Document Control and Version Management: Maintain document version control, revision histories, and audit trails across multiple client programs. Ensure changes to notices, certifications, affidavits, and other program documents are accurately tracked, reviewed, approved, and maintained.

· Regulatory and Business Compliance: Ensure program documentation and configuration requirements align with applicable state and local legislation, established business rules, internal policies, and system capabilities. Identify potential discrepancies or compliance concerns and coordinate appropriate review and resolution.

· Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to improve requirements gathering, documentation management, workflow efficiency, and implementation practices to support scalable, repeatable, and high-quality program delivery.

Qualifications and Experience

· Minimum of five years of experience in a client-facing role involving business requirements management, business analysis, client configuration, implementation coordination, or a related discipline supporting technology implementations.

· Demonstrated experience partnering with Engineering, Software Development, Product, or other technical teams to translate business requirements into system configurations, technical specifications, or implementation deliverables.

· Exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to identify discrepancies, validate complex information, maintain accurate records, and consistently produce high-quality work.
